6.7: Now let alone the work of the house of God: let the rulers of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its place.
6.8: Also a decree has been made by me, if haply ye may do somewhat in concert with the elders of the Jews for the building of that house of God: to wit, out of the king's property, even the tributes beyond the river, let there be money to defray the expenses carefully granted to those men, so that they be not hindered.
6.9: And whatever need there may be , ye shall give both the young of bulls and rams, and lambs for whole-burnt-offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, oil:—let it be given them according to the word of the priests that are in Jerusalem, day by day whatsoever they shall ask;
6.10: that they may offer sweet savours to the God of heaven, and that they may pray for the life of the king and his sons.
6.11: And a decree has been made by me, that every man who shall alter this word, timber shall be pulled down from his house, and let him be lifted up and slain upon it, and his house shall be confiscated.
6.12: And may the God whose name dwells there, overthrow every king and people who shall stretch out his hand to alter or destroy the house of God which is in Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree; let it be diligently attended to .
6.13: Then Thanthanai the governor on this side beyond the river, Satharbuzanai, and his fellow-servants, according to that which king Darius sent, so they did diligently.
6.14: And the elders of the Jews and the Levites built, at the prophecy of Aggæus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo: and they built up, and finished it , by the decree of the God of Israel, and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Arthasastha, kings of the Persians.
6.15: And they finished this house by the third day of the month Adar, which is the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
6.16: And the children of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of the house of God with gladness.
6.17: And they offered for the dedication of the house of God a hundred calves, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, twelve kids of the goats for a sin-offering for all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
6.18: And they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their separate orders, for the services of God in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
6.19: And the children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
6.20: For the priests and Levites were purified, all were clean to a man, and they slew the passover for all the children of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.
6.21: And the children of Israel ate the passover, even they that were of the captivity, and every one who separated himself to them from the uncleanness of the nations of the land, to seek the Lord God of Israel.
6.22: And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with gladness, because the Lord made them glad, and he turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.

7.1: Now after these things, in the reign of Arthasastha king of the Persians, came up Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias, the son of Chelcias,
7.2: the son of Selum, the son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob,
7.3: the son of Samarias, the son of Esria, the son of Mareoth,
7.4: the son of Zaraia, the son of Ozias, the son of Bokki,
7.5: the son of Abisue, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the first priest.
7.6: This Esdras went up out of Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel gave: and the king gave him leave , for the hand of the Lord his God was upon him in all things which he sought.
7.7: And some of the children of Israel went up, and some of the priests, and of the Levites, and the singers, and the door-keepers, and the Nathinim, to Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Arthasastha the king.
7.8: And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, this was the seventh year of the king.
7.9: For in the first day of the first month he began the going up from Babylon, and in the first day of the fifth month they came to Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was upon him.
7.10: For Esdras had determined in his heart to seek the law, and to do and teach the ordinances and judgments in Israel.
7.11: And this is the copy of the order which Arthasastha gave to Esdras the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the commandments of the Lord, and of his ordinances to Israel.
7.12: Arthasastha, king of kings, to Esdras, the scribe of the law of the Lord God of heaven, Let the order and the answer be accomplished.
7.13: A decree is made by me, that every one who is willing in my kingdom of the people of Israel, and of the priests and Levites, to go to Jerusalem, be permitted to go with thee.
7.14: One has been sent from the king and the seven councillors, to visit Judea and Jerusalem, according to the law of their God that is in thine hand.
7.15: And for the house of the Lord there have been sent silver and gold, which the king and the councillors have freely given to the God of Israel, who dwells in Jerusalem.
7.16: And all the silver and gold, whatsoever thou shalt find in all the land of Babylon, with the freewill-offering of the people, and the priests that offer freely for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.
7.17: And as for every one that arrives there , speedily order him by this letter to bring calves, rams, lambs, and their meat-offerings, and their drink-offerings; and thou shalt offer them on the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
7.18: And whatever it shall seem good to thee and to thy brethren to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do as it is pleasing to your God.
7.19: And deliver the vessels that are given thee for the service of the house of God, before God in Jerusalem.
7.20: And as to the rest of the need of the house of thy God, thou shalt give from the king's treasure-houses,
7.21: and from me, whatever it shall seem good to thee to give. I king Arthasastha have made a decree for all the treasuries that are in the country beyond the river, that whatever Esdras the priest and scribe of the God of heaven may ask you, it shall be done speedily,
7.22: to the amount of a hundred talents of silver, and a hundred measures of wheat, and a hundred baths of wine, and a hundred baths of oil, and salt without reckoning.
7.23: Let whatever is in the decree of the God of heaven, be done: take heed lest any one make an attack on the house of the God of heaven, lest at any time there should be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons.
7.24: Also this has been declared to you, with respect to all the priests, and Levites, the singers, porters, Nathinim and ministers of the house of God, let no tribute be paid to thee; thou shalt not have power to oppress them.
7.25: And thou, Esdras, as the wisdom of God is in thy hand, appoint scribes and judges, that they may judge for all the people beyond the river, all that know the law of the Lord thy God; and ye shall make it known to him that knows not.
7.26: And whosoever shall not do the law of God, and the law of the king readily, judgment shall be taken upon him, whether for death or for chastisement, or for a fine of his property, or casting into prison.
7.27: Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, who has put it thus into the heart of the king, to glorify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem;
7.28: and has given me favour in the eyes of the king, and of his councillors, and all the rulers of the king, the exalted ones. And I was strengthened according to the good hand of God upon me, and I gathered chief men of Israel to go up with me.

8.1: And these are the heads of their families, the leaders that went up with me in the reign of Arthasastha the king of Babylon.
8.2: Of the sons of Phinees; Gerson: of the sons of Ithamar; Daniel: of the sons of David; Attus.
8.3: Of the sons of Sachania, and of the sons of Phoros; Zacharias: and with him a company of a hundred and fifty.
8.4: Of the sons of Phaath-Moab; Eliana the son of Saraia, and with him two hundred that were males.
8.5: And of the sons of Zathoes; Sechenias the son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males.
8.6: And of the sons of Adin; Obeth the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males.
8.7: And of the sons of Elam; Isæas the son of Athelia, and with him seventy males.
8.8: And of the sons of Saphatia; Zabadias the son of Michael, and with him eighty males.
8.9: And of the sons of Joab; Abadia the son of Jeiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males.
8.10: And of the sons of Baani; Selimuth the son of Josephia, and with him a hundred and sixty males.
8.11: And of the sons of Babi; Zacharias the son of Babi, and with him twenty-eight males.
8.12: And of the sons of Asgad; Joanan the son of Accatan, and with him a hundred and ten males.
8.13: And of the sons of Adonicam were the last, and these were their names, Eliphalat, Jeel, and Samæa, and with them sixty males.
8.14: And of the sons of Baguæ, Uthai, and Zabud, and with him seventy males.
8.15: And I gathered them to the river that comes to Evi, and we encamped there three days: and I reviewed the people and the priests, and found none of the sons of Levi there.
8.16: And I sent men of understanding to Eleazar, to Ariel, to Semeias, and to Alonam, and to Jarib, and to Elnatham, and to Nathan, and to Zacharias, and to Mesollam, and to Joarim, and to Elnathan.
8.17: And I forwarded them to the rulers with the money of the place, and I put words in their mouth to speak to their brethren the Athinim with the money of the place, that they should bring us singers for the house of our God.
8.18: And they came to us, as the good hand of our God was upon us, even a man of understanding of the sons of Mooli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and at the commencement came his sons and his brethren, eighteen.
8.19: And Asebia, and Isaia of the sons of Merari, his brethren and his sons, twenty.
8.20: And of the Nathinim, whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites there were two hundred and twenty Nathinim; all were gathered by their names.
8.21: And I proclaimed there a fast, at the river Aüe, that we should humble ourselves before our God, to seek of him a straight way for us, and for our children, and for all our property.
8.22: For I was ashamed to ask of the king a guard and horsemen to save us from the enemy in the way: for we had spoken to the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all that seek him, for good; but his power and his wrath are upon all that forsake him.
8.23: So we fasted, and asked of our God concerning this; and he hearkened to us.
8.24: And I gave charge to twelve of the chiefs of the priests, to Saraia, to Asabia, and ten of their brethren with them.
8.25: And I weighed to them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of the first-fruits of the house of our God, which the king, and his councillors, and his princes, and all Israel that were found, had dedicated.
8.26: I even weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and a hundred silver vessels, and a hundred talents of gold;
8.27: and twenty golden bowls, weighing about a thousand drachms, and superior vessels of fine shining brass, precious as gold.
8.28: And I said to them, Ye are holy to the Lord; and the vessels are holy; and the silver and the gold are freewill-offerings to the Lord God of our fathers.
8.29: Be watchful and keep them, until ye weigh them before the chief priests and the Levites, and the chiefs of families in Jerusalem, at the chambers of the house of the Lord.
8.30: So the priests and the Levites took the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to bring to Jerusalem into the house of our God.
8.31: And we departed from the river of Aüe on the twelfth day of the first month, to come to Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and delivered us from the hand of the enemy and adversary in the way.
8.32: And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three days.
8.33: And it came to pass on the fourth day that we weighed the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, in the house of our God, into the hand of Merimoth the son of Uria the priest; and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinees, and with them Jozabad the son of Jesus, and Noadia the son of Banaia, the Levites.
8.34: All things were reckoned by number and weight, and the whole weight was written down .
8.35: At that time the children of the banishment that came from the captivity offered whole-burnt-offerings to the God of Israel, twelve calves for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve goats for a sin-offering: all whole-burnt-offerings to the Lord.
8.36: And they gave the king's mandate to the king's lieutenants, and the governors beyond the river: and they honoured the people and the house of God.

9.1: And when these things were finished, the princes drew near to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands in their abominations, even the Chananite, the Ethite, the Pherezite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, and the Moserite and the Amorite.
9.2: For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and their sons; and the holy seed has passed among the nations of the lands, and the hand of the rulers has been first in this transgression.
9.3: And when I heard this thing, I rent my garments, and trembled, and plucked some of the hairs of my head and of my beard, and sat down mourning.
9.4: Then there assembled to me all that followed the word of the God of Israel, on account of the transgression of the captivity; and I remained mourning until the evening sacrifice.
9.5: And at the evening sacrifice I rose up from my humiliation; and when I had rent my garments, then I trembled, and I bow myself on my knees, and spread out my hands to the Lord God,
9.6: and I said, O Lord, I am ashamed and confounded, O my God, to lift up my face to thee: for our transgressions have abounded over our head, and our trespasses have increased even to heaven.
9.7: From the days of our fathers we have been in a great trespass until this day: and because of our iniquities we, and our kings, and our children, have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the Gentiles by the sword, and by captivity, and by spoil, and with shame of our face, as at this day.
9.8: And now our God has dealt mercifully with us, so as to leave us to escape, and to give us an establishment in the place of his sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes, and to give a little quickening in our servitude.
9.9: For we are slaves, yet in our servitude the Lord our God has not deserted us; and he has extended favour to us in the sight of the kings of the Persians, to give us a quickening, that they should raise up the house of our God, and restore the desolate places of it, and to give us a fence in Juda and Jerusalem.
9.10: What shall we say, our God, after this? for we have forsaken thy commandments,
9.11: which thou hast given us by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying, The land, into which ye go to inherit it, is a land subject to disturbance by the removal of the people of the nations for their abominations, wherewith they have filled it from one end to the other by their uncleannesses.
9.12: And now give not your daughters to their sons, and take not of their daughters for your sons, neither shall ye seek their peace or their good for ever: that ye may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and transmit it as an inheritance to your children for ever.
9.13: And after all that is come upon us because of our evil deeds, and our great trespass, it is clear that there is none such as our God, for thou hast lightly visited our iniquities, and given us deliverance;
9.14: whereas we have repeatedly broken thy commandments, and intermarried with the people of the lands: be not very angry with us to our utter destruction, so that there should be no remnant or escaping one.
9.15: O Lord God of Israel, thou art righteous; for we remain yet escaped, as at this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee on this account.

10.1: So when Esdras had prayed, and when he had confessed, weeping and praying before the house of God, a very great assembly of Israel came together to him, men and women and youths; for the people wept, and wept aloud.
10.2: And Sechenias the son of Jeel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Esdras, We have broken covenant with our God, and have taken strange wives of the nations of the land: yet now there is patience of hope to Israel concerning this thing.
10.3: Now then let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives, and their offspring, as thou shalt advise:
10.4: arise, and alarm them with the commands of our God; and let it be done according to the law. Rise up, for the matter is upon thee; and we are with thee: be strong and do.
10.5: Then Esdras arose, and caused the rulers, the priests, and Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they would do according to this word: and they swore.
10.6: And Esdras rose up from before the house of God, and went to the treasury of Joanan the son of Elisub; he even went thither: he ate no bread, and drank no water; for he mourned over the unfaithfulness of them of the captivity.
10.7: And they made proclamation throughout Juda and Jerusalem to all the children of the captivity, that they should assemble at Jerusalem, saying ,
10.8: Every one who shall not arrive within three days, as is the counsel of the rulers and the elders, all his substance shall be forfeited, and he shall be separated from the congregation of the captivity.
10.9: So all the men of Juda and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days. This was the ninth month: on the twentieth day of the month all the people sat down in the street of the house of the Lord, because of their alarm concerning the word, and because of the storm.
10.10: And Esdras the priest arose, and said to them, Ye have broken covenant, and have taken strange wives, to add to the trespass of Israel.
10.11: Now therefore give praise to the Lord God of our fathers, and do that which is pleasing in his sight: and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land, and from the strange wives.
10.12: Then all the congregation answered and said, This thy word is powerful upon us to do it.
10.13: But the people is numerous, and the season is stormy, and there is no power to stand without, and the work is more than enough for one day or for two; for we have greatly sinned in this matter.
10.14: Let now our rulers stand, and for all those in our cities who have taken strange wives, let them come at appointed times, and with them elders from every several city, and judges, to turn away the fierce wrath of our God from us concerning this matter.
10.15: Only Jonathan the son of Asael, and Jazias the son of Thecoe were with me concerning this; and Mesollam, and Sabbathai the Levite helped them.
10.16: And the children of the captivity did thus: and Esdras the priest, and heads of families according to their house were separated, and all by their names, for they returned in the first day of the tenth month to search out the matter.
10.17: And they made an end with all the men who had taken strange wives by the first day of the first month.
10.18: And there were found some of the sons of the priests who had taken strange wives: of the sons of Jesus the son of Josedec, and his brethren; Maasia, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gadalia.
10.19: And they pledged themselves to put away their wives, and offered a ram of the flock for a trespass-offering because of their trespass.
10.20: And of the sons of Emmer; Anani, and Zabdia.
10.21: And of the sons of Eram; Masael, and Elia, and Samaia, and Jeel, and Ozia.
10.22: And of the sons of Phasur; Elionai, Maasia, and Ismael, and Nathanael, and Jozabad, and Elasa.
10.23: And of the Levites; Jozabad, and Samu, and Colia (he is Colitas,) and Phetheia, and Judas, and Eliezer.
10.24: And of the singers; Elisab: and of the porters; Solmen, and Telmen, and Oduth.
10.25: Also of Israel: of the sons of Phoros; Ramia, and Azia, and Melchia, and Meamin, and Eleazar, and Asabia, and Banaia.
10.26: And of the sons of Helam; Matthania, and Zacharia, and Jaïel, and Abdia, and Jarimoth, and Elia.
10.27: And of the sons of Zathua; Elionai, Elisub, Matthanai, and Armoth, and Zabad, and Oziza.
10.28: And of the sons of Babei; Joanan, Anania, and Zabu, and Thali.
10.29: And of the sons of Banui; Mosollam, Maluch, Adaias, Jasub, and Saluia, and Remoth.
10.30: And of the sons of Phaath Moab; Edne, and Chalel, and Banaia, Maasia, Matthania, Beseleel, and Banui, and Manasse.
10.31: And of the sons of Eram; Eliezer, Jesia, Melchia, Samaias, Semeon,
10.32: Benjamin, Baluch, Samaria.
10.33: And of the sons of Asem; Metthania, Matthatha, Zadab, Eliphalet, Jerami, Manasse, Semei.
10.34: And of the sons of Bani; Moodia, Amram, Uel,
10.38: and so did the children of Banui, and the children of Semei,
10.39: and Selemia, and Nathan, and Adaia,
10.43: Of the sons of Nabu; Jael, Matthanias, Zabad, Zebennas, Jadai, and Joel, and Banaia.
10.44: All these had taken strange wives, and had begotten sons of them.

11.1: The words of Neemias the son of Chelcia. And it came to pass in the month Chaseleu, of the twentieth year, that I was in Susan the palace.
11.2: And Anani, one of my brethren, came, he and some men of Juda; and I asked them concerning those that had escaped, who had been left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
11.3: And they said to me, The remnant, even those that are left of the captivity, are there in the land, in great distress and reproach: and the walls of Jerusalem are thrown down, and its gates are burnt with fire.
11.4: And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned for several days, and continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
11.5: And I said, Nay, I pray thee, O Lord God of heaven, the mighty, the great and terrible, keeping thy covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to those that keep his commandments:
11.6: let now thine ear be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee at this time, this day both day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and make confession for the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and the house of my father have sinned.
11.7: We have altogether broken covenant with thee, and we have not kept the commandments, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which thou didst command thy servant Moses.
11.8: Remember, I pray thee, the word wherewith thou didst charge thy servant Moses, saying, If ye break covenant with me , I will disperse you among the nations.
11.9: But if ye turn again to me, and keep my commandments, and do them; if ye should be scattered under the utmost bound of heaven, thence will I gather them, and I will bring them into the place which I have chosen to cause my name to dwell there.
11.10: Now they are thy servants and thy people, whom thou hast redeemed with thy great power, and with thy strong hand.
11.11: Turn not away , I pray thee, O Lord, but let thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and cause him to find mercy in the sight of this man. Now I was the king's cup-bearer.

12.1: And it came to pass in the month Nisan of the twentieth year of king Arthasastha, that the wine was before me: and I took the wine, and gave it to the king: and there was not another before him.
12.2: And the king said to me, Why is thy countenance sad, and dost thou not control thyself? and now this is nothing but sorrow of heart. Then I was very much alarmed,
12.3: and I said to the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, forasmuch as the city, even the home of the sepulchres of my fathers, has been laid waste, and her gates have been devoured with fire?
12.4: And the king said to me, For what dost thou ask thus? So I prayed to the God of heaven.
12.5: And I said to the king, If it seem good to the king, and if thy servant shall have found favour in thy sight, I ask that thou wouldest send him into Juda, to the city of the sepulchres of my fathers; then will I rebuild it.
12.6: And the king, and his concubine that sat next to him, said to me, For how long will thy journey be, and when wilt thou return? and the proposal was pleasing before the king, and he sent me away, and I appointed him a time.
12.7: And I said to the king, If it seem good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the river, so as to forward me till I come to Juda;
12.8: and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the garden which belongs to the king, that he may give me timber to cover the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for the house into which I shall enter. And the king gave to me, according as the good hand of God was upon me .
12.9: And I came to the governors beyond the river, and I gave them the king's letters. (Now the king had sent with me captains of the army and horsemen.)
12.10: And Sanaballat the Aronite heard it , and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and it was grievous to them that a man was come to seek good for the children of Israel.
12.11: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
12.12: And I rose up by night, I and a few men with me; and I told no man what God put into my heart to do with Israel; and there was no beast with me, except the beast which I rode upon.
12.13: And I went forth by the gate of the valley by night, and to the mouth of the well of fig trees, and to the dung-gate: and I mourned over the wall of Jerusalem which they were destroying, and her gates were devoured with fire.
12.14: And I passed on to the fountain gate, and to the king's pool; and there was no room for the beast to pass under me.
12.15: And I went up by the wall of the brook by night, and mourned over the wall, and passed through the gate of the valley, and returned.
12.16: And the sentinels knew not why I went, nor what I was doing; and until that time I told it not to the Jews, or to the priests, or to the nobles, or to the captains, or to the rest of the men who wrought the works.
12.17: Then I said to them, Ye see this evil, in which we are, how Jerusalem is desolate, and her gates have been set on fire: come, and let us build throughout the wall of Jerusalem, and we shall be no longer a reproach.
12.18: And I told them of the hand of God which was good upon me, also about the words of the king which he spoke to me: and I said, Let us arise and build. And their hands were strengthened for the good work .
12.19: And Sanaballat the Aronite, and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and Gesam the Arabian, heard it , and they laughed us to scorn, and came to us, and said, What is this thing that ye are doing? are ye revolting against the king?
12.20: And I answered them, and said to them, The God of heaven, he shall prosper us, and we his servants are pure, and we will build: but ye have no part, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.

13.1: Then Eliasub the high priest, and his brethren the priests, rose up, and built the sheep-gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even to the tower of the hundred they sanctified it , to the tower of Anameel.
13.2: And they builded by the side of the men of Jericho, and by the side of the sons of Zacchur, the son of Amari.
13.3: And the sons of Asana built the fish-gate; they roofed it, and covered in its doors, and bolts, and bars.
13.4: And next to them the order reached to Ramoth the son of Uria, the son of Accos, and next to them Mosollam son of Barachias the son of Mazebel took his place: and next to them Sadoc the son of Baana took his place.
13.5: And next to them the Thecoim took their place; but the Adorim applied not their neck to their service.
13.6: And next to them repaired Maltias the Gabaonite, and Evaron the Meronothite, the men of Gabaon and Maspha, to the throne of the governor on this side the river.
13.8: And next to him Oziel the son of Arachias of the smiths, carried on the repairs: and next to them Ananias the son of one of the apothecaries repaired, and they finished Jerusalem to the broad wall.
13.9: And next to them repaired Raphæa the son of Sur, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem.
13.10: And next to them repaired Jedaia the son of Eromaph, and that in front of his house: and next to him repaired Attuth son of Asabania.
13.11: And next to him repaired Melchias son of Heram, and Asub son of Phaat Moab, even to the tower of the furnaces.
13.12: And next to him repaired Sallum the son of Alloes, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem, he and his daughters.
13.13: Anun and the inhabitants of Zano repaired the gate of the valley: they built it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the dung-gate.
13.14: And Melchia the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district round about Bethaccharim, repaired the dung-gate, he and his sons; and they covered it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
13.15: But Solomon the son of Choleze repaired the gate of the fountain, the ruler of part of Maspha; he built it, and covered it, and set up its doors and its bars, and the wall of the pool of the skins by the meadow of the king, and as far as the steps that lead down from the city of David.
13.16: After him repaired Neemias son of Azabuch, ruler of half the district round about Bethsur, as far as the garden of David's sepulchre, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men.
13.17: After him repaired the Levites, even Raum the son of Bani: next to him repaired Asabia, ruler of half the district round about Keila, in his district.
13.18: And after him repaired his brethren, Benei son of Enadad, ruler of half the district round about Keila.
13.19: And next to him repaired Azur the son of Joshua, ruler of Masphai, another portion of the tower of ascent, where it meets the corner.
13.20: After him repaired Baruch the son of Zabu, a second portion, from the corner as far as the door of the house of Eliasub the high priest.
13.21: After him repaired Meramoth the son of Uria the son of Accos, a second part from the door of the house of Eliasub to the end of the house of Eliasub.
13.22: And after him repaired the priests, the men of Ecchechar.
13.23: And after him repaired Benjamin and Asub over against their house: and after him repaired Azarias son of Maasias the son of Ananias, the parts near to his house.
13.24: After him repaired Bani the son of Adad, another portion from the house of Azaria as far as the corner and to the turning,
13.25: of Phalach the son of Uzai, opposite the corner, and where is also the tower that projects from the king's house, even the upper one of the prison-house: and after him repaired Phadæa the son of Phoros.
13.26: And the Nathinim dwelt in Ophal, as far as the garden of the water-gate eastward, and there is the projecting tower.
13.27: And after them the Thecoim repaired, another portion opposite the great projecting tower, even as far as the wall of Ophla.
13.28: The priests repaired above the horse-gate, every man over against his own house.
13.29: And after him Sadduc the son of Emmer repaired opposite his own house: and after him repaired Samæa son of Sechenia, guard of the east-gate.
13.30: After him repaired Anania son of Selemia, and Anom, the sixth son of Seleph, another portion: after him Mesulam the son of Barachia repaired over against his treasury.
13.31: After him repaired Melchia the son of Sarephi as far as the house of the Nathinim, and the chapmen over against the gate of Maphecad, and as far as the steps of the corner.
13.32: And between that and the sheep-gate the smiths and chapmen repaired.
13.33: Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, that it was grievous to him, and he was very angry, and railed against the Jews.
13.34: And he said before his brethren (that is the army of the Samaritans) Is it true that these Jews are building their city? do they indeed offer sacrifices? will they prevail? and will they this day restore the stones, after they have been burnt and made a heap of rubbish?
13.35: And Tobias the Ammanite came near to him, and said to them, Do they sacrifice or eat in their place? shall not a fox go up and pull down their wall of stones?
13.36: Hear, O our God, for we have become a scorn; and return thou their reproach upon their head, and make them a scorn in a land of captivity,
13.37: and do not cover their iniquity.

14.1: But it came to pass, when Sanaballat and Tobia, and the Arabians, and the Ammanites, heard that the building of the walls of Jerusalem was advancing, and that the breaches began to be stopped, that it appeared very grievous to them.
14.2: And all of them assembled together, to come to fight against Jerusalem, and to destroy it utterly.
14.3: So we prayed to our God and set watchmen against them day and night, because of them.
14.4: And Juda said, The strength of the enemies is broken, yet there is much rubbish, and we shall not be able to build the wall.
14.5: And they that afflicted us said, They shall not know, and they shall not see, until we come into the midst of them, and slay them, and cause the work to cease.
14.6: And it came to pass, when the Jews who lived near them came, that they said to us, They are coming up against us from every quarter.
14.7: So I set men in the lowest part of the place behind the wall in the lurking-places, I even set the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
14.8: And I looked, and arose, and said to the nobles, and to the captains, and to the rest of the people, Be not afraid of them: remember our great and terrible God, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.
14.9: And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it was made known to us, and God had frustrated their counsel, that we all returned to the wall, every man to his work.
14.10: And it came to pass from that day that half of them that had been driven forth, wrought the work, and half of them kept guard; and there were spears, and shields, and bows, and breast-plates, and rulers behind the whole house of Juda,
14.11: even of them that were building the wall:—and those who carried the burdens were under arms: each with one hand wrought his work, and with the other held his dart.
14.12: And the builders wrought each man having his sword girt upon his loins, and so they built: and the trumpeter with his trumpet next to him.
14.13: And I said to the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, The work is great and abundant, and we are dispersed upon the wall, each at a great distance from his brother.
14.14: In whatsoever place ye shall hear the sound of the cornet, thither gather yourselves together to us; and our God shall fight for us.
14.15: So we continued labouring at the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appeared.
14.16: And at that time I said to the people, Lodge ye every man with his servant in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be a watch-time to you, and the day a work-time.
14.17: And I was there , and the watchmen behind me, and there was not a man of us that put off his garments.

15.1: And the cry of the people and their wives was great against their brethren the Jews.
15.2: And some said, We are numerous with our sons and our daughters; so we will take corn, and eat, and live.
15.3: And some said, As to our fields and vineyards and houses, let us pledge them , and we will take corn, and eat.
15.4: And some said, We have borrowed money for the king's tributes:—our fields, and our vineyards, and houses are pledged .
15.5: And now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children are as their children: yet, behold, we are reducing our sons and our daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are enslaved: and there is no power of our hands, for our fields and our vineyards belong to the nobles.
15.6: And I was much grieved as I heard their cry and these words.
15.7: And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended against the nobles, and the princes, and I said to them, Should every man demand of his brother what ye demand? And I appointed against them a great assembly,
15.8: and I said to them, We of our free-will have redeemed our brethren the Jews that were sold to the Gentiles; and do ye sell your brethren? and shall they be delivered to us? And they were silent, and found no answer.
15.9: And I said, The thing which ye do is not good; ye will not so walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the Gentiles our enemies.
15.10: Both my brethren, and my acquaintances, and I, have lent them money and corn: let us now leave off this exaction.
15.11: Restore to them, I pray, as at this day, their fields, and their vineyards, and their olive-yards, and their houses, and bring forth to them corn and wine and oil of the money.
15.12: And they said, We will restore, and we will not exact of them; we will do thus as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and bound them by oath to do according to this word.
15.13: And I shook out my garment, and said, So may God shake out every man who shall not keep to this word, from his house, and from his labours, he shall be even thus shaken out, as an outcast and empty. And all the congregation said, Amen, and they praised the Lord: and the people did this thing.
15.14: From the day that he charged me to be their ruler in the land of Juda, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years, I and my brethren ate not provision extorted from them.
15.15: But as for the former acts of extortion wherein those who were before me oppressed them, they even took of them their last money, forty didrachms for bread and wine; and the very outcasts of them exercised authority over the people: but I did not so, because of the fear of God.
15.16: Also in the work of the wall I treated them not with rigour, I bought not land: and all that were gathered together came thither to the work.
15.17: And the Jews, to the number of a hundred and fifty men, besides those coming to us from the nations round about, were at my table.
15.18: And there came to me for one day one calf, and I had six choice sheep and a goat; and every ten days wine in abundance of all sorts: yet with these I required not the bread of extortion, because the bondage was heavy upon this people.
15.19: Remember me, O God, for good, in all that I have done to this people.

16.1: Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat, and Tobias, and Gesam the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies, heard that I had built the wall, and that there was no opening left therein; ( but hitherto I had not set up the doors on the gates;)
16.2: that Sanaballat and Gesam sent to me, saying, Come and let us meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono. But they were plotting to do me mischief.
16.3: So I sent messengers to them, saying, I am doing a great work, and I shall not be able to come down, lest the work should cease: as soon as I shall have finished it, I will come down to you.
16.4: And they sent to me again to this effect; and I sent them word accordingly.
16.5: Then Sanaballat sent his servant to me with an open letter in his hand.
16.6: And in it was written, It has been reported among the Gentiles that thou and the Jews are planning to revolt: therefore thou art building the wall, and thou wilt be a king to them.
16.7: And moreover thou hast appointed prophets to thyself, that thou mightest dwell in Jerusalem as a king over Juda: and now these words will be reported to the king. Now then, come, let us take counsel together.
16.8: And I sent to him, saying, It has not happened according to these words, even as thou sayest, for thou framest them falsely out of thy heart.
16.9: For all were trying to alarm us, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from this work, and it shall not be done. Now therefore I have strengthened my hands.
16.10: And I came into the house of Semei the son of Dalaia the son of Metabeel, and he was shut up; and he said, Let us assemble together in the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut the doors of it; for they are coming by night to slay thee.
16.11: And I said, Who is the man that shall enter into the house, that he may live?
16.12: And I observed, and, behold, God had not sent him, for the prophecy was a fable devised against me:
16.13: and Tobias and Sanaballat had hired against me a multitude, that I might be frightened, and do this, and sin, and become to them an ill name, that they might reproach me.
16.14: Remember, O God, Tobias and Sanaballat, according to these their deeds, and the prophetess Noadia, and the rest of the prophets who tried to alarm me.
16.15: So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days.
16.16: And it came to pass, when all our enemies heard of it , that all the nations round about us feared, and great alarm fell upon them, and they knew that it was of our God that this work should be finished.
16.17: And in those days letters came to Tobias from many nobles of Juda, and those of Tobias came to them.
16.18: For many in Juda were bound to him by oath, because he was son-in-law of Sechenias the son of Herae; and Jonan his son had taken the daughter of Mesulam the son of Barachia to wife.
16.19: And they reported his words to me, and carried out my words to him: and Tobias sent letters to terrify me.

17.1: And it came to pass, when the wall was built, and I had set up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Levites were appointed,
17.2: that I gave charge to Ananias my brother, and Ananias the ruler of the palace, over Jerusalem: for he was a true man, and one that feared God beyond many.
17.3: And I said to them, The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened till sunrise; and while they are still watching, let the doors be shut, and bolted; and set watches of them that dwell in Jerusalem, every man at his post, and every man over against his house.
17.4: Now the city was wide and large; and the people were few in it, and the houses were not built.
17.5: And God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, into companies: and I found a register of the company that came up first, and I found written in it as follows:
17.6: Now these are the children of the country, that came up from captivity, of the number which Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried away, and they returned to Jerusalem and to Juda, every man to his city;
17.7: with Zorobabel, and Jesus, and Neemia, Azaria, and Reelma, Naemani, Mardochæus, Balsan, Maspharath, Esdra, Boguia, Inaum, Baana, Masphar, men of the people of Israel.
17.8: The children of Phoros, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two.
17.9: The children of Saphatia, three hundred and seventy-two.
17.10: The children of Era, six hundred and fifty-two.
17.11: The children of Phaath Moab, with the children of Jesus and Joab, two thousand six hundred and eighteen.
17.12: The children of Ælam, a thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
17.13: The children of Zathuia, eight hundred and forty-five.
17.14: The children of Zacchu, seven hundred and sixty.
17.15: The children of Banui, six hundred and forty-eight.
17.16: The children of Bebi, six hundred and twenty-eight.
17.17: The children of Asgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-two.
17.18: The children of Adonicam, six hundred and sixty-seven.
17.19: The children of Bagoi, two thousand and sixty-seven.
17.20: The children of Edin, six hundred and fifty-five.
17.21: The children of Ater, the son of Ezekias, ninety-eight.
17.22: The children of Esam, three hundred and twenty-eight.
17.23: The children of Besei, three hundred and twenty-four.
17.24: The children of Ariph, a hundred and twelve: the children of Asen, two hundred and twenty-three.
17.26: The children of Bæthalem, a hundred and twenty-three: the children of Atopha, fifty-six.
17.27: The children of Anathoth, a hundred and twenty-eight.
17.29: The men of Cariatharim, Caphira, and Beroth, seven hundred and forty-three.
17.30: The men of Arama and Gabaa, six hundred and twenty.
17.31: The men of Machemas, a hundred and twenty-two.
17.32: The men of Bæthel and Ai, a hundred and twenty-three.
17.33: The men of Nabia, a hundred and fifty-two.
17.34: The men of Elamaar, one thousand two hundred and fifty-two.
17.35: The children of Eram, three hundred and twenty.
17.36: The children of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five.
17.37: The children of Lodadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-one.
17.38: The children of Sanana, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.

17.52: the children of Besi, the children of Meinon, the children of Nephosasi,

17.54: the children of Basaloth, the children of Mida, the children of Adasan,

17.57: The children of the servants of Solomon; the children of Sutei, the children of Sapharat, the children of Pherida,
