34.16: They tempted me, they sneered at me most contemptuously, they gnashed their teeth upon me.
34.17: O Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? Deliver my soul from their mischief, mine only-begotten one from the lions.
34.18: I will give thanks to thee even in a great congregation: in an abundant people I will praise thee.
34.19: Let not them that are mine enemies without a cause rejoice against me; who hate me for nothing, and wink with their eyes.
34.20: For to me they spoke peaceably, but imagined deceits in their anger.
34.21: And they opened wide their mouth upon me; they said, Aha, aha, our eyes have seen it .
34.22: Thou hast seen it , O Lord: keep not silence: O Lord, withdraw not thyself from me.
34.23: Awake, O Lord, and attend to my judgment, even to my cause, my God and my Lord.
34.24: Judge me, O Lord, according to thy righteousness, O Lord my God; and let them not rejoice against me.
34.25: Let them not say in their hearts, Aha, aha, it is pleasing to our soul: neither let them say, We have devoured him.
34.26: Let them be confounded and ashamed together that rejoice at my afflictions: let them be clothed with shame and confusion that speak great swelling words against me.
34.27: Let them that rejoice in my righteousness exult and be glad: and let them say continually, The Lord be magnified, who desire the peace of his servant.
34.28: And my tongue shall meditate on thy righteousness, and on thy praise all the day.

35.1: For the end, by David the servant of the Lord.
35.2: The transgressor, that he may sin, says within himself, that there is no fear of God before his eyes.
35.3: For he has dealt craftily before him, to discover his iniquity and hate it.
35.4: The words of his mouth are transgression and deceit: he is not inclined to understand how to do good.
35.5: He devises iniquity on his bed; he gives himself to every evil way; and does not abhor evil.
35.6: O Lord, thy mercy is in the heaven; and thy truth reaches to the clouds.
35.7: Thy righteousness is as the mountains of God, thy judgments are as a great deep: O Lord, thou wilt preserve men and beasts.
35.8: How hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God! so the children of men shall trust in the shelter of thy wings.
35.9: They shall be fully satisfied with the fatness of thine house; and thou shalt cause them to drink of the full stream of thy delights.
35.10: For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light we shall see light.
35.11: Extend thy mercy to them that know thee; and thy righteousness to the upright in heart.
35.12: Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of sinners move me.
35.13: There have all the workers of iniquity fallen: they are cast out, and shall not be able to stand.

36.1: A Psalm of David. Fret not thyself because of evil-doers, neither be envious of them that do iniquity.
36.2: For they shall soon be withered as the grass, and shall soon fall away as the green herbs.
36.3: Hope in the Lord, and do good; and dwell on the land, and thou shalt be fed with the wealth of it.
36.4: Delight thyself in the Lord; and he shall grant thee the requests of thine heart.
36.5: Disclose thy way to the Lord, and hope in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
36.6: And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noon-day.
36.7: Submit thyself to the Lord, and supplicate him: fret not thyself because of him that prospers in his way, at the man that does unlawful deeds.
36.8: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself so as to do evil.
36.9: For evil-doers shall be destroyed: but they that wait on the Lord, they shall inherit the land.
36.10: And yet a little while, and the sinner shall not be, and thou shalt seek for his place, and shalt not find it .
36.11: But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
36.12: The sinner will watch for the righteous, and gnash his teeth upon him.
36.13: But the Lord shall laugh at him: for he foresees that his day will come.
36.14: Sinners have drawn their swords, they have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy one, and to slay the upright in heart.
36.15: Let their sword enter into their own heart, and their bows be broken.
36.16: A little is better to the righteous than abundant wealth of sinners.
36.17: For the arms of sinners shall be broken; but the Lord supports the righteous.
36.18: The Lord knows the ways of the perfect; and their inheritance shall be for ever.
36.19: They shall not be ashamed in an evil time; and in days of famine they shall be satisfied.
36.20: For the sinners shall perish; and the enemies of the Lord at the moment of their being honoured and exalted have utterly vanished like smoke.
36.21: The sinner borrows, and will not pay again: but the righteous has compassion, and gives.
36.22: For they that bless him shall inherit the earth; and they that curse him shall be utterly destroyed.
36.23: The steps of a man are rightly ordered by the Lord: and he will take pleasure in his way.
36.24: When he falls, he shall not be ruined: for the Lord supports his hand.
36.25: I was once young, indeed I am now old; yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
36.26: He is merciful, and lends continually; and his seed shall be blessed.
36.27: Turn aside from evil, and do good; and dwell for ever.
36.28: For the Lord loves judgment, and will not forsake his saints; they shall be preserved for ever: the blameless shall be avenged, but the seed of the ungodly shall be utterly destroyed.
36.29: But the righteous shall inherit the earth, and dwell upon it for ever.
36.30: The mouth of the righteous will meditate wisdom, and his tongue will speak of judgment.
36.31: The law of his God is in his heart; and his steps shall not slide.
36.32: The sinner watches the righteous, and seeks to slay him.
36.33: But the Lord will not leave him in his hands, nor by any means condemn him when he is judged.
36.34: Wait on the Lord, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are destroyed, thou shalt see it .
36.35: I saw the ungodly very highly exalting himself, and lifting himself up like the cedars of Libanus.
36.36: Yet I passed by, and lo! he was not: and I sought him, but his place was not found.
36.37: Maintain innocence, and behold uprightness: for there is a remnant to the peaceable man.
36.38: But the transgressors shall be utterly destroyed together: the remnants of the ungodly shall be utterly destroyed.
36.39: But the salvation of the righteous is of the Lord; and he is their defender in the time of affliction.
36.40: And the Lord shall help them, and deliver them: and he shall rescue them from sinners, and save them, because they have hoped in him.

37.1: A Psalm of David for remembrance concerning the Sabbath-day.
37.2: O Lord, rebuke me not in thy wrath, neither chasten me in thine anger.
37.3: For thy weapons are fixed in me, and thou hast pressed thy hand heavily upon me.
37.4: For there is no health in my flesh because of thine anger; there is no peace to my bones because of my sins.
37.5: For my transgressions have gone over mine head: they have pressed heavily upon me like a weighty burden.
37.6: My bruises have become noisome and corrupt, because of my foolishness.
37.7: I have been wretched and bowed down continually: I went with a mourning countenance all the day.
37.8: For my soul is filled with mockings; and there is no health in my flesh.
37.9: I have been afflicted and brought down exceedingly: I have roared for the groaning of my heart.
37.10: But all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hidden from thee.
37.11: My heart is troubled, my strength has failed me; and the light of mine eyes is not with me.
37.12: My friends and my neighbours drew near before me, and stood still; and my nearest of kin stood afar off.
37.13: While they pressed hard upon me that sought my soul: and they that sought my hurt spoke vanities, and devised deceits all the day.
37.14: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and was as a dumb man not opening his mouth.
37.15: And I was as a man that hears not, and who has no reproofs in his mouth.
37.16: For I hoped in thee, O Lord: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.
37.17: For I said, Lest mine enemies rejoice against me: for when my feet were moved, they spoke boastingly against me.
37.18: For I am ready for plagues, and my grief is continually before me.
37.19: For I will declare mine iniquity, and be distressed for my sin.
37.20: But mine enemies live, and are mightier than I: and they that hate me unjustly are multiplied.
37.21: They that reward evil for good slandered me; because I followed righteousness.
37.22: Forsake me not, O Lord my God: depart not from me.
37.23: Draw nigh to my help, O Lord of my salvation.

38.1: For the end, a Song of David, to Idithun.
38.2: I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I set a guard on my mouth, while the sinner stood in my presence.
38.3: I was dumb, and humbled myself, and kept silence from good words ; and my grief was renewed.
38.4: My heart grew hot within me, and a fire would kindle in my meditation: I spoke with my tongue,
38.5: O Lord, make me to know mine end, and the number of my days, what it is; that I may know what I lack.
38.6: Behold, thou hast made my days old; and my existence is as nothing before thee: nay, every man living is altogether vanity. Pause.
38.7: Surely man walks in a shadow; nay, he is disquieted in vain: he lays up treasures, and knows not for whom he shall gather them.
38.8: And now what is my expectation? is it not the Lord? and my ground of hope is with thee. Pause.
38.9: Deliver me from all my transgressions: thou hast made me a reproach to the foolish.
38.10: I was dumb, and opened not my mouth; for thou art he that made me.
38.11: Remove thy scourges from me: I have fainted by reason of the strength of thine hand.
38.12: Thou chastenest man with rebukes for iniquity, and thou makest his life to consume away like a spider's web: nay, every man is disquieted in vain. Pause.
38.13: O Lord, hearken to my prayer and my supplication: attend to my tears: be not silent, for I am a sojourner in the land, and a stranger, as all my fathers were .
38.14: Spare me, that I may be refreshed, before I depart, and be no more.

39.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
39.2: I waited patiently for the Lord; and he attended to me, and hearkened to my supplication.
39.3: And he brought me up out of a pit of misery, and from miry clay: and he set my feet on a rock, and ordered my goings aright.
39.4: And he put a new song into my mouth, even a hymn to our God: many shall see it , and fear, and shall hope in the Lord.
39.5: Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord, and who has not regarded vanities and false frenzies.
39.6: O Lord my God, thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, and in thy thoughts there is none who shall be likened to thee: I declared and spoke of them : they exceeded number.
39.7: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; but a body hast thou prepared me: whole-burnt-offering and sacrifice for sin thou didst not require.
39.8: Then I said, Behold, I come: in the volume of the book it is written concerning me,
39.9: I desired to do thy will, O my God, and thy law in the midst of mine heart.
39.10: I have preached righteousness in the great congregation; lo! I will not refrain my lips; O Lord, thou knowest my righteousness.
39.11: I have not hid thy truth within my heart, and I have declared thy salvation; I have not hid thy mercy and thy truth from the great congregation.
39.12: But thou, Lord, remove not thy compassion far from me; thy mercy and thy truth have helped me continually.
39.13: For innumerable evils have encompassed me; my transgressions have taken hold of me, and I could not see; they are multiplied more than the hairs of my head; and my heart has failed me.
39.14: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me; O Lord, draw nigh to help me.
39.15: Let those that seek my soul, to destroy it, be ashamed and confounded together; let those that wish me evil be turned backward and put to shame.
39.16: Let those that say to me, Aha, aha, quickly receive shame for their reward.
39.17: Let all those that seek thee, O Lord, exult and rejoice in thee; and let them that love thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified.
39.18: But I am poor and needy; the Lord will take care of me; thou art my helper, and my defender, O my God, delay not.

40.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
40.2: Blessed is the man who thinks on the poor and needy: the Lord shall deliver him in an evil day.
40.3: May the Lord preserve him and keep him alive, and bless him on the earth, and not deliver him into the hands of his enemy.
40.4: May the Lord help him upon the bed of his pain; thou hast made all his bed in his sickness.
40.5: I said, O Lord, have mercy upon me; heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.
40.6: Mine enemies have spoken evil against me, saying , When shall he die, and his name perish?
40.7: And if he came to see me , his heart spoke vainly; he gathered iniquity to himself; he went forth and spoke in like manner.
40.8: All my enemies whispered against me; against me they devised my hurt.
40.9: They denounced a wicked word against me, saying , Now that he lies, shall he not rise up again?
40.10: For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, lifted up his heel against me.
40.11: But thou, O Lord, have compassion upon me, and raise me up, and I shall requite them.
40.12: By this I know that thou hast delighted in me, because mine enemy shall not rejoice over me.
40.13: But thou didst help me because of mine innocence, and hast established me before thee for ever.
40.14: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. So be it, so be it.

41.1: For the end, a Psalm for instruction, for the sons of Core.
41.2: As the hart earnestly desires the fountains of water, so my soul earnestly longs for thee, O God.
41.3: My soul has thirsted for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
41.4: My tears have been bread to me day and night, while they daily said to me, Where is thy God?
41.5: I remembered these things, and poured out my soul in me, for I will go to the place of thy wondrous tabernacle, even to the house of God, with a voice of exultation and thanksgiving and of the sound of those who keep festival.
41.6: Wherefore art thou very sad, O my soul? and wherefore dost thou trouble me? hope in God; for I will give thanks to him; he is the salvation of my countenance.
41.7: O my God, my soul has been troubled within me: therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan, and of the Ermonites, from the little hill.
41.8: Deep calls to deep at the voice of thy cataracts: all thy billows and thy waves have gone over me.
41.9: By day the Lord will command his mercy, and manifest it by night: with me is prayer to the God of my life.
41.10: I will say to God, Thou art my helper; why hast thou forgotten me? wherefore do I go sad of countenance, while the enemy oppresses me ?
41.11: While my bones were breaking, they that afflicted me reproached me; while they said to me daily, Where is thy God?
41.12: Wherefore art thou very sad, O my soul? and wherefore dost thou trouble me? hope in God; for I will give thanks to him; he is the health of my countenance, and my God.

42.1: A Psalm of David. Judge me, O God, and plead my cause, against an ungodly nation: deliver me from the unjust and crafty man.
42.2: For thou, O God, art my strength: wherefore hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sad of countenance, while the enemy oppresses me ?
42.3: Send forth thy light and thy truth: they have led me, and brought me to thy holy mountain, and to thy tabernacles.
42.4: And I will go in to the altar of God, to God who gladdens my youth: I will give thanks to thee on the harp, O God, my God.
42.5: Wherefore art thou very sad, O my soul? and wherefore dost thou trouble me? Hope in God; for I will give thanks to him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.

43.1: For the end, a Psalm for instruction, for the sons of Core.
43.2: O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us, the work which thou wroughtest in their days, in the days of old.
43.3: Thine hand utterly destroyed the heathen, and thou didst plant them: thou didst afflict the nations, and cast them out.
43.4: For they inherited not the land by their own sword, and their own arm did not deliver them; but thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou wert well pleased in them.
43.5: Thou art indeed my King and my God, who commandest deliverances for Jacob.
43.6: In thee will we push down our enemies, and in thy name will we bring to nought them that rise up against us.
43.7: For I will not trust in my bow, and my sword shall not save me.
43.8: For thou hast saved us from them that afflicted us, and hast put to shame them that hated us.
43.9: In God will we make our boast all the day, and to thy name will we give thanks for ever. Pause.
43.10: But now thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and thou wilt not go forth with our hosts.
43.11: Thou hast turned us back before our enemies; and they that hated us spoiled for themselves.
43.12: Thou madest us as sheep for meat; and thou scatteredst us among the nations.
43.13: Thou hast sold thy people without price, and there was no profit by their exchange.
43.14: Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
43.15: Thou hast made us a proverb among the Gentiles, a shaking of the head among the nations.
43.16: All the day my shame is before me, and the confusion of my face has covered me,
43.17: because of the voice of the slanderer and reviler; because of the enemy and avenger.
43.18: All these things are come upon us: but we have not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt unrighteously in thy covenant.
43.19: And our heart has not gone back; but thou hast turned aside our paths from thy way.
43.20: For thou hast laid us low in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death has covered us.
43.21: If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a strange god; shall not God search these things out?
43.22: for he knows the secrets of the heart.
43.23: For, for thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for slaughter.
43.24: Awake, wherefore sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, and do not cast us off for ever.
43.25: Wherefore turnest thou thy face away, and forgettest our poverty and our affliction?
43.26: For our soul has been brought down to the dust; our belly has cleaved to the earth.
43.27: Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for thy name's sake.

44.1: For the end, for alternate strains by the sons of Core; for instruction, a Song concerning the beloved.
44.2: My heart has uttered a good matter: I declare my works to the king: my tongue is the pen of a quick writer.
44.3: Thou art more beautiful than the sons of men: grace has been shed forth on thy lips: therefore God has blessed thee for ever.
44.4: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O Mighty One, in thy comeliness, and in thy beauty;
44.5: and bend thy bow , and prosper, and reign, because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall guide thee wonderfully.
44.6: Thy weapons are sharpened, Mighty One, (the nations shall fall under thee) they are in the heart of the king's enemies.
44.7: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of righteousness.
44.8: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity: therefore God, thy God, has anointed thee with the oil of gladness beyond thy fellows.
44.9: Myrrh, and stacte, and cassia are exhaled from thy garments, and out of the ivory palaces,
44.10: with which kings' daughters have gladdened thee for thine honour: the queen stood by on thy right hand, clothed in vesture wrought with gold, and arrayed in divers colours.
44.11: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear; forget also thy people, and thy father's house.
44.12: Because the king has desired thy beauty; for he is thy Lord.
44.13: And the daughter of Tyre shall adore him with gifts; the rich of the people of the land shall supplicate thy favour.
44.14: All her glory is that of the daughter of the king of Esebon, robed as she is in golden fringed garments,
44.15: in embroidered clothing : virgins shall be brought to the king after her: her fellows shall be brought to thee.
44.16: They shall be brought with gladness and exultation: they shall be led into the king's temple.
44.17: Instead of thy fathers children are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.
44.18: They shall make mention of thy name from generation to generation: therefore shall the nations give thanks to thee for ever, even for ever and ever.

45.1: For the end, for the sons of Core; a Psalm concerning secret things.
45.2: God is our refuge and strength, a help in the afflictions that have come heavily upon us.
45.3: Therefore will we not fear when the earth is troubled, and the mountains are removed into the depths of the seas.
45.4: Their waters have roared and been troubled, the mountains have been troubled by his might. Pause.
45.5: The flowings of the river gladden the city of God: the Most High has sanctified his tabernacle.
45.6: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her with his countenance.
45.7: The nations were troubled, the kingdoms tottered: he uttered his voice, the earth shook.
45.8: The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper. Pause.
45.9: Come, and behold the works of the Lord, what wonders he has achieved on the earth.
45.10: Putting an end to wars as for the ends of the earth; he will crush the bow, and break in pieces the weapon, and burn the bucklers with fire.
45.11: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.
45.12: The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper.

46.1: For the end, a Psalm for the sons of Core.
46.2: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout to God with a voice of exultation.
46.3: For the Lord most high is terrible; he is a great king over all the earth.
46.4: He has subdued the peoples under us, and the nations under our feet.
46.5: He has chosen out his inheritance for us, the beauty of Jacob which he loved. Pause.
46.6: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with a sound of a trumpet.
46.7: Sing praises to our God, sing praises: sing praises to our King, sing praises.
46.8: For God is king of all the earth: sing praises with understanding.
46.9: God reigns over the nations: God sits upon the throne of his holiness.
46.10: The rulers of the people are assembled with the God of Abraam: for God's mighty ones of the earth have been greatly exalted.

47.1: A Psalm of praise for the sons of Core on the second day of the week.
47.2: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
47.3: The city of the great King is well planted on the mountains of Sion, with the joy of the whole earth, on the sides of the north.
47.4: God is known in her palaces, when he undertakes to help her.
47.5: For, behold, the kings of the earth were assembled, they came together.
47.6: They saw, and so they wondered: they were troubled, they were moved.
47.7: Trembling took hold on them: there were the pangs as of a woman in travail.
47.8: Thou wilt break the ships of Tharsis with a vehement wind.
47.9: As we have heard, so have we also seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God has founded it for ever. Pause.
47.10: We have thought of thy mercy, O God, in the midst of thy people.
47.11: According to thy name, O God, so is also thy praise to the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.
47.12: Let mount Sion rejoice, let the daughters of Judæa exult, because of thy judgments, O Lord.
47.13: Go round about Sion, and encompass her: tell ye her towers.
47.14: Mark ye well her strength, and observe her palaces; that ye may tell the next generation.
47.15: For this is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide for evermore.

48.1: For the end, a Psalm for the sons of Core.
48.2: Hear these words, all ye nations, hearken, all ye that dwell upon the earth:
48.3: both the sons of mean men, and sons of great men; the rich and poor man together.
48.4: My mouth shall speak of wisdom; and the meditation of my heart shall bring forth understanding.
48.5: I will incline mine ear to a parable: I will open my riddle on the harp.
48.6: Wherefore should I fear in the evil day? the iniquity of my heel shall compass me.
48.7: They that trust in their strength, and boast themselves in the multitude of their wealth—
48.8: A brother does not redeem, shall a man redeem? he shall not give to God a ransom for himself,
48.9: or the price of the redemption of his soul, though he labour for ever,
48.10: and live to the end, so that he should not see corruption.
48.11: When he shall see wise men dying, the fool and the senseless one shall perish together; and they shall leave their wealth to strangers.
48.12: And their sepulchres are their houses for ever, even their tabernacles to all generations: they have called their lands after their own names.
48.13: And man being in honour, understands not: he is compared to the senseless cattle, and is like to them.
48.14: This their way is an offence to them: yet afterwards men will commend their sayings. Pause.
48.15: They have laid them as sheep in Hades; death shall feed on them; and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning, and their help shall fail in Hades from their glory.
48.16: But God shall deliver my soul from the power of Hades, when he shall receive me. Pause.
48.17: Fear not when a man is enriched, and when the glory of his house is increased.
48.18: For he shall take nothing when he dies; neither shall his glory descend with him.
48.19: For his soul shall be blessed in his life: he shall give thanks to thee when thou dost well to him.
48.20: Yet he shall go in to the generation of his fathers; he shall never see light.
48.21: Man that is in honour, understands not: he is compared to the senseless cattle, and is like them.

49.1: A Psalm for Asaph. The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun to the going down thereof .
49.2: Out of Sion comes the excellence of his beauty.
49.3: God, our God, shall come manifestly, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall be kindled before him, and round about him there shall be a very great tempest.
49.4: He shall summon the heaven above, and the earth, that he may judge his people.
49.5: Assemble ye his saints to him, those that have engaged in a covenant with him upon sacrifices.
49.6: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge. Pause.
49.7: Hear, my people, and I will speak to thee, O Israel: and I will testify to thee: I am God, thy God.
49.8: I will not reprove thee on account of thy sacrifices; for thy whole-burnt-offerings are before me continually.
49.9: I will take no bullocks out of thine house, nor he-goats out of thy flocks.
49.10: For all the wild beasts of the thicket are mine, the cattle on the mountains, and oxen.
49.11: I know all the birds of the sky; and the beauty of the field is mine.
49.12: If I should be hungry, I will not tell thee: for the world is mine, and the fulness of it.
49.13: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
49.14: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise; and pay thy vows to the Most High.
49.15: And call upon me in the day of affliction; and I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me. Pause.
49.16: But to the sinner God has said, Why dost thou declare my ordinances, and take up my covenant in thy mouth?
49.17: Whereas thou hast hated instruction, and hast cast my words behind thee .
49.18: If thou sawest a thief, thou rannest along with him, and hast cast in thy lot with adulterers.
49.19: Thy mouth has multiplied wickedness, and thy tongue has framed deceit.
49.20: Thou didst sit and speak against thy brother, and didst scandalise thy mother's son.
49.21: These things thou didst, and I kept silence: thou thoughtest wickedly that I should be like thee; but I will reprove thee, and set thine offences before thee.
49.22: Now consider these things, ye that forget God, lest he rend you , and there be no deliverer.
49.23: The sacrifice of praise will glorify me: and that is the way wherein I will shew to him the salvation of God.

50.1: For the end, a Psalm of David,
50.2: when Nathan the prophet came to him, when he had gone in to Bersabee.
50.3: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy great mercy; and according to the multitude of thy compassions blot out my transgression.
50.4: Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
50.5: For I am conscious of mine iniquity; and my sin is continually before me.
50.6: Against thee only have I sinned, and done evil before thee: that thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.
50.7: For, behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins did my mother conceive me.
50.8: For, behold, thou lovest truth: thou hast manifested to me the secret and hidden things of thy wisdom.
50.9: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be purified: thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.
50.10: Thou shalt cause me to hear gladness and joy: the afflicted bones shall rejoice.
50.11: Turn away thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
50.12: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit in my inward parts.
50.13: Cast me not away from thy presence; and remove not thy Holy Spirit from me.
50.14: Restore to me the joy of thy salvation: establish me with thy directing Spirit.
50.15: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and ungodly men shall turn to thee.
50.16: Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation: and my tongue shall joyfully declare thy righteousness.
50.17: O Lord, thou shalt open my lips; and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
50.18: For if thou desiredst sacrifice, I would have given it : thou wilt not take pleasure in whole-burnt-offerings.
50.19: Sacrifice to God is a broken spirit: a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.
50.20: Do good, O Lord, to Sion in thy good pleasure; and let the walls of Jerusalem be built.
50.21: Then shalt thou be pleased with a sacrifice of righteousness, offering, and whole-burnt-sacrifices: then shall they offer calves upon thine altar.

51.1: For the end, a Psalm of instruction by David,
51.2: when Doec the Idumean came and told Saul, and said to him, David is gone to the house of Abimelech.
51.3: Why dost thou, O mighty man, boast of iniquity in thy mischief? All the day
51.4: thy tongue has devised unrighteousness; like a sharpened razor thou hast wrought deceit.
51.5: Thou hast loved wickedness more than goodness; unrighteousness better than to speak righteousness. Pause.
51.6: Thou hast loved all words of destruction, and a deceitful tongue.
51.7: Therefore may God destroy thee for ever, may he pluck thee up and utterly remove thee from thy dwelling, and thy root from the land of the living. Pause.
51.8: And the righteous shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say,
51.9: Behold the man who made not God his help; but trusted in the abundance of his wealth, and strengthened himself in his vanity.
51.10: But I am as a fruitful olive in the house of God: I have trusted in the mercy of God for ever, even for evermore.
51.11: I will give thanks to thee for ever, for thou hast done it : and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.

52.1: For the end, a Psalm of David upon Maeleth, of instruction.
52.2: The fool has said in his heart, There is no God. They have corrupted themselves , and become abominable in iniquities: there is none that does good.
52.3: God looked down from heaven upon the sons of men, to see if there were any that understood, or sought after God.
52.4: They have all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that does good, there is not even one.
52.5: Will none of the workers of iniquity know, who devour my people as they would eat bread? they have not called upon God. There were they greatly afraid, where there was no fear:
52.6: for God has scattered the bones of the men-pleasers; they were ashamed, for God despised them.
52.7: Who will bring the salvation of Israel out of Sion? When the Lord turns the captivity of his people, Jacob shall exult, and Israel shall be glad.

53.1: For the end, among the Hymns of instruction by David,
53.2: when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, Lo, is not David hid with us?
53.3: Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy might.
53.4: O God, hear my prayer; hearken to the words of my mouth.
53.5: For strangers have risen up against me, and mighty men have sought my life: they have not set God before them. Pause.
53.6: For lo! God assists me; and the Lord is the helper of my soul.
53.7: He shall return evil to mine enemies; utterly destroy them in thy truth.
53.8: I will willingly sacrifice to thee: I will give thanks to thy name, O Lord; for it is good.
53.9: For thou hast delivered me out of all affliction, and mine eye has seen my desire upon mine enemies.

54.1: For the end, among Hymns of instruction by David.
54.2: Hearken, O God, to my prayer; and disregard not my supplication.
54.3: Attend to me, and hearken to me: I was grieved in my meditation, and troubled;
54.4: because of the voice of the enemy, and because of the oppression of the sinner: for they brought iniquity against me, and were wrathfully angry with me.
54.5: My heart was troubled within me; and the fear of death fell upon me.
54.6: Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
54.7: And I said, O that I had wings as those of a dove! then would I flee away, and be at rest.
54.8: Lo! I have fled afar off, and lodged in the wilderness. Pause.
54.9: I waited for him that should deliver me from distress of spirit and tempest.
54.10: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen iniquity and gainsaying in the city.
54.11: Day and night he shall go round about it upon its walls: iniquity and sorrow and unrighteousness are in the midst of it;
54.12: and usury and craft have not failed from its streets.
54.13: For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if one who hated me had spoken vauntingly against me, I would have hid myself from him.
54.14: But thou, O man likeminded, my guide, and my acquaintance,
54.15: who in companionship with me sweetened our food: we walked in the house of God in concord.
54.16: Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into Hades, for iniquity is in their dwellings, in the midst of them.
54.17: I cried to God, and the Lord hearkened to me.
54.18: Evening, and morning, and at noon I will declare and make known my wants : and he shall hear my voice.
54.19: He shall deliver my soul in peace from them that draw nigh to me: for they were with me in many cases .
54.20: God shall hear, and bring them low, even he that has existed from eternity. Pause. For they suffer no reverse, and therefore they have not feared God.
54.21: He has reached forth his hand for retribution; they have profaned his covenant.
54.22: They were scattered at the anger of his countenance, and his heart drew nigh them. His words were smoother than oil, yet are they darts.
54.23: Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee; he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
54.24: But thou, O God, shalt bring them down to the pit of destruction; bloody and crafty men shall not live out half their days; but I will hope in thee, O Lord.

55.1: For the end, concerning the people that were removed from the sanctuary, by David for a memorial, when the Philistines caught him in Geth.
55.2: Have mercy upon me, O God; for man has trodden me down; all the day long he warring has afflicted me.
55.3: Mine enemies have trodden me down all the day from the dawning of the day; for there are many warring against me.
55.4: They shall be afraid, but I will trust in thee.
55.5: In God I will praise my words; all the day have I hoped in God; I will not fear what flesh shall do to me.
55.6: All the day long they have abominated my words; all their devices are against me for evil.
55.7: They will dwell near and hide themselves ; they will watch my steps, accordingly as I have waited patiently in my soul.
55.8: Thou wilt on no account save them; thou wilt bring down the people in wrath.
55.9: O God, I have declared my life to thee; thou hast set my tears before thee, even according to thy promise.
55.10: Mine enemies shall be turned back, in the day wherein I shall call upon thee; behold, I know that thou art my God.
55.11: In God will I praise his word; in the Lord will I praise his saying.
55.12: I have hoped in God; I will not be afraid of what man shall do to me.
55.13: The vows of thy praise, O God, which I will pay, are upon me.
55.14: For thou hast delivered my soul from death, and my feet from sliding, that I should be well-pleasing before God in the land of the living.

56.1: For the end. Destroy not: by David, for a memorial, when he fled from the presence of Saul to the cave.
56.2: Have mercy, upon me, O God, have mercy upon me: for my soul has trusted in thee: and in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, until the iniquity have passed away.
56.3: I will cry to God most high; the God who has benefited me. Pause.
56.4: He sent from heaven and saved me; he gave to reproach them that trampled on me: God has sent forth his mercy and his truth;
56.5: and he has delivered my soul from the midst of lions' whelps: I lay down to sleep, though troubled. As for the sons of men, their teeth are arms and missile weapons, and their tongue a sharp sword.
56.6: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; and thy glory above all the earth.
56.7: They have prepared snares for my feet, and have bowed down my soul: they have dug a pit before my face, and fallen into it themselves . Pause.
56.8: My heart, O God, is ready, my heart is ready: I will sing, yea will sing psalms.
56.9: Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I will awake early.
56.10: O Lord, I will give thanks to thee among the nations: I will sing to thee among the Gentiles.
56.11: For thy mercy has been magnified even to the heavens, and thy truth to the clouds.
56.12: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; and thy glory above all the earth.

57.1: For the end. Destroy not: by David, for a memorial.
57.2: If ye do indeed speak righteousness, then do ye judge rightly, ye sons of men.
57.3: For ye work iniquities in your hearts in the earth: your hands plot unrighteousness.
57.4: Sinners have gone astray from the womb: they go astray from the belly: they speak lies.
57.5: Their venom is like that of a serpent; as that of a deaf asp, and that stops her ears;
57.6: which will not hear the voice of charmers, nor heed the charm prepared skilfully by the wise.
57.7: God has crushed their teeth in their mouth: God has broken the cheek-teeth of the lions.
57.8: They shall utterly pass away like water running through: he shall bend his bow till they shall fail.
57.9: They shall be destroyed as melted wax: the fire has fallen and they have not seen the sun.
57.10: Before your thorns feel the white thorn, he shall swallow you up as living, as in his wrath.
57.11: The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance of the ungodly: he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.
57.12: And a man shall say, Verily then there is a reward for the righteous: verily there is a God that judges them in the earth.

58.1: For the end. Destroy not: by David for a memorial, when Saul sent, and watched his house to kill him.
58.2: Deliver me from mine enemies, O God; and ransom me from those that rise up against me.
58.3: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from bloody men.
58.4: For, behold, they have hunted after my soul; violent men have set upon me: neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord.
58.5: Without iniquity I ran and directed my course aright : awake to help me, and behold.
58.6: And thou, Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, draw nigh to visit all the heathen; pity not any that work iniquity. Pause.
58.7: They shall return at evening, and hunger like a dog, and go round about the city.
58.8: Behold, they shall utter a voice with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips; for who, say they , has heard?
58.9: But thou, Lord, wilt laugh them to scorn; thou wilt utterly set at nought all the heathen.
58.10: I will keep my strength, looking to thee; for thou, O God, art my helper.
58.11: As for my God, his mercy shall go before me: my God will shew me vengeance on mine enemies.
58.12: Slay them not, lest they forget thy law; scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord, my defender.
58.13: For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips, let them be even taken in their pride.
58.14: And for their cursing and falsehood shall utter destruction be denounced: they shall fall by the wrath of utter destruction, and shall not be; so shall they know that the God of Jacob is Lord of the ends of the earth. Pause.
58.15: They shall return at evening, and be hungry as a dog, and go round about the city.
58.16: They shall be scattered hither and thither for meat; and if they be not satisfied, they shall even murmur.
58.17: But I will sing to thy strength, and in the morning will I exult in thy mercy; for thou hast been my supporter, and my refuge in the day of mine affliction.
58.18: Thou art my helper; to thee, my God, will I sing; thou art my supporter, O my God, and my mercy.

59.1: For the end, for them that shall yet be changed; for an inscription by David for instruction,
59.2: when he had burned Mesopotamia of Syria, and Syria Sobal, and Joab had returned and smitten in the valley of salt twelve thousand.
59.3: O God, thou hast rejected and destroyed us; thou hast been angry, yet hast pitied us.
59.4: Thou hast shaken the earth, and troubled it; heal its breaches, for it has been shaken.
59.5: Thou hast shewn thy people hard things: thou hast made us drink the wine of astonishment.
59.6: Thou hast given a token to them that fear thee, that they might flee from the bow. Pause.
59.7: That thy beloved ones may be delivered; save with thy right hand, and hear me.
59.8: God has spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice, and divide Sicima, and measure out the valley of tents.
59.9: Galaad is mine, and Manasse is mine; and Ephraim is the strength of my head;
59.10: Judas is my king; Moab is the caldron of my hope; over Idumea will I stretch out my shoe; the Philistines have been subjected to me.
59.11: Who will lead me into the fortified city? who will guide me as far as Idumea?
59.12: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our forces?
59.13: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the deliverance of man.
59.14: In God will we do valiantly; and he shall bring to nought them that harass us.

60.1: For the end, among the Hymns of David.
60.2: O God, hearken to my petition; attend to my prayer.
60.3: From the ends of the earth have I cried to thee, when my heart was in trouble: thou liftedst me up on a rock, thou didst guide me:
60.4: because thou wert my hope, a tower of strength from the face of the enemy.
60.5: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever; I will shelter myself under the shadow of thy wings. Pause.
60.6: For thou, O God, hast heard my prayers; thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.
60.7: Thou shalt add days to the days of the king; thou shalt lengthen his years to all generations.
60.8: He shall endure for ever before God: which of them will seek out his mercy and truth?
60.9: So will I sing to thy name for ever and ever, that I may daily perform my vows.

61.1: For the end, a Psalm of David for Idithun.
61.2: Shall not my soul be subjected to God? for of him is my salvation.
61.3: For he is my God and my Saviour; my helper, I shall not be moved very much.
61.4: How long will ye assault a man? ye are all slaughtering as with a bowed wall and a broken hedge.
61.5: They only took counsel to set at nought mine honour: I ran in thirst: with their mouth they blessed, but with their heart they cursed. Pause.
61.6: Nevertheless do thou, my soul, be subjected to God; for of him is my patient hope.
61.7: For he is my God and my Saviour; my helper, I shall not be moved.
61.8: In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.
61.9: Hope in him, all ye congregation of the people; pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper. Pause.
61.10: But the sons of men are vain; the sons of men are false, so as to be deceitful in the balances; they are all alike formed out of vanity.
61.11: Trust not in unrighteousness, and lust not after robberies: if wealth should flow in, set not your heart upon it.
61.12: God has spoken once, and I have heard these two things, that power is of God;
61.13: and mercy is thine, O Lord; for thou wilt recompense every one according to his works.

62.1: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Idumea.
62.2: O God, my God, I cry to thee early; my soul has thirsted for thee: how often has my flesh longed after thee, in a barren and trackless and dry land!
62.3: Thus have I appeared before thee in the sanctuary, that I might see thy power and thy glory.
62.4: For thy mercy is better than life: my lips shall praise thee.
62.5: Thus will I bless thee during my life: I will lift up my hands in thy name.
62.6: Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness; and my joyful lips shall praise thy name.
62.7: Forasmuch as I have remembered thee on my bed: in the early seasons I have meditated on thee.
62.8: For thou hast been my helper, and in the shelter of thy wings will I rejoice.
62.9: My soul has kept very close behind thee: thy right hand has upheld me.
62.10: But they vainly sought after my soul; they shall go into the lowest parts of the earth.
62.11: They shall be delivered up to the power of the sword; they shall be portions for foxes.
62.12: But the king shall rejoice in God; every one that swears by him shall be praised; for the mouth of them that speak unjust things has been stopped.

63.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
63.2: Hear my prayer, O God, when I make my petition to thee; deliver my soul from fear of the enemy.
63.3: Thou hast sheltered me from the conspiracy of them that do wickedly; from the multitude of them that work iniquity;
63.4: who have sharpened their tongues as a sword; they have bent their bow maliciously;
63.5: to shoot in secret at the blameless; they will shoot him suddenly, and will not fear.
63.6: They have set up for themselves an evil matter, they have given counsel to hide snares; they have said, Who shall see them?
63.7: They have searched out iniquity; they have wearied themselves with searching diligently, a man shall approach and the heart is deep,
63.8: and God shall be exalted, their wounds were caused by the weapon of the foolish children,
63.9: and their tongues have set him at nought, all that saw them were troubled;
63.10: and every man was alarmed, and they related the works of God, and understood his deeds.
63.11: The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord, and hope on him, and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

64.1: For the end, a Psalm and Song of David.
64.2: Praise becomes thee, O God, in Sion; and to thee shall the vow be performed.
64.3: Hear my prayer; to thee all flesh shall come.
64.4: The words of transgressors have overpowered us; but do thou pardon our sins.
64.5: Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and adopted; he shall dwell in thy courts; we shall be filled with the good things of thy house; thy temple is holy.
64.6: Thou art wonderful in righteousness. Hearken to us, O God our Saviour; the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are on the sea afar off:
64.7: who dost establish the mountains in thy strength, being girded about with power;
64.8: who troublest the depth of the sea, the sounds of its waves.
64.9: The nations shall be troubled, and they that inhabit the ends of the earth shall be afraid of thy signs; thou wilt cause the outgoings of morning and evening to rejoice.
64.10: Thou hast visited the earth, and saturated it; thou hast abundantly enriched it. The river of God is filled with water; thou hast prepared their food, for thus is the preparation of it .
64.11: Saturate her furrows, multiply her fruits; the crop springing up shall rejoice in its drops.
64.12: Thou wilt bless the crown of the year because of thy goodness; and thy plains shall be filled with fatness.
64.13: The mountains of the wilderness shall be enriched; and the hills shall gird themselves with joy.
64.14: The rams of the flock are clothed with wool , and the valleys shall abound in corn; they shall cry aloud, yea they shall sing hymns.

65.1: For the end, a Song of a Psalm of resurrection. Shout unto God, all the earth.
65.2: O sing praises to his name; give glory to his praise.
65.3: Say unto God, How awful are thy works! through the greatness of thy power thine enemies shall lie to thee.
65.4: Let all the earth worship thee, and sing to thee; let them sing to thy name. Pause.
65.5: Come and behold the works of God; he is terrible in his counsels beyond the children of men.
65.6: Who turns the sea into dry land; they shall go through the river on foot; there shall we rejoice in him,
65.7: who by his power is Lord over the age, his eyes look upon the nations; let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves. Pause.
65.8: Bless our God, ye Gentiles, and make the voice of his praise to be heard;
65.9: who quickens my soul in life, and does not suffer my feet to be moved.
65.10: For thou, O God, hast proved us; thou hast tried us with fire as silver is tried.
65.11: Thou broughtest us into the snare; thou laidest afflictions on our back.
65.12: Thou didst mount men upon our heads; we went through fire and water; but thou broughtest us out into a place of refreshment.
65.13: I will go into thine house with whole-burnt-offerings; I will pay thee my vows,
65.14: which my lips framed, and my mouth uttered in my affliction.
65.15: I will offer to thee whole-burnt-sacrifices full of marrow, with incense and rams; I will sacrifice to thee oxen with goats. Pause.
65.16: Come, hear, and I will tell, all ye that fear God, how great things he has done for my soul.
65.17: I cried to him with my mouth, and exalted him with my tongue.
65.18: If I have regarded iniquity in my heart, let not the Lord hearken to me .
65.19: Therefore God has hearkened to me; he has attended to the voice of my prayer.
65.20: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

66.1: For the end, a Psalm of David among the Hymns.
66.2: God be merciful to us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us. Pause.
66.3: That men may know thy way on the earth, thy salvation among all nations.
66.4: Let the nations, O God, give thanks to thee; let all the nations give thanks to thee.
66.5: Let the nations rejoice and exult, for thou shalt judge the peoples in equity, and shalt guide the nations on the earth. Pause.
66.6: Let the peoples, O God, give thanks to thee; let all the peoples give thanks to thee.
66.7: The earth has yielded her fruit; let God, our God, bless us.
66.8: Let God bless us; and let all the ends of the earth fear him.

67.1: For the end, a Psalm of a Song by David.
67.2: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; and let them that hate him flee from before him.
67.3: As smoke vanishes, let them vanish: as wax melts before the fire, so let the sinners perish from before God.
67.4: But let the righteous rejoice; let them exult before God: let them be delighted with joy.
67.5: Sing to God, sing praises to his name: make a way for him that rides upon the west (the Lord is his name) and exult before him. They shall be troubled before the face of him,
67.6: who is the father of the orphans, and judge of the widows: such is God in his holy place.
67.7: God settles the solitary in a house; leading forth prisoners mightily, also them that act provokingly, even them that dwell in tombs.
67.8: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, when thou wentest through the wilderness; Pause:
67.9: the earth quaked, yea, the heavens dropped water at the presence of the God of Sina, at the presence of the God of Israel.
67.10: O God, thou wilt grant to thine inheritance a gracious rain; for it was weary, but thou didst refresh it.
67.11: Thy creatures dwell in it: thou hast in thy goodness prepared for the poor.
67.12: The Lord God will give a word to them that preach it in a great company.
67.13: The king of the forces of the beloved, of the beloved, will even grant them for the beauty of the house to divide the spoils.
67.14: Even if ye should lie among the lots, ye shall have the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her breast with yellow gold.
67.15: When the heavenly One scatters kings upon it, they shall be made snow-white in Selmon.
67.16: The mountain of God is a rich mountain; a swelling mountain, a rich mountain.
67.17: Wherefore do ye conceive evil , ye swelling mountains? this is the mountain which God has delighted to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever.
67.18: The chariots of God are ten thousand fold, thousands of rejoicing ones: the Lord is among them, in Sina, in the holy place.
67.19: Thou art gone up on high, thou hast led captivity captive, thou hast received gifts for man, yea, for they were rebellious, that thou mightest dwell among them.
67.20: Blessed be the Lord God, blessed be the Lord daily; and the God of our salvation shall prosper us. Pause.
67.21: Our God is the God of salvation; and to the Lord belong the issues from death.
67.22: But God shall crush the heads of his enemies; the hairy crown of them that go on in their trespasses.
67.23: The Lord said, I will bring again from Basan, I will bring my people again through the depths of the sea.
67.24: That thy foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongue of thy dogs be stained with that of thine enemies.
67.25: Thy goings, O God, have been seen; the goings of my God, the king, in the sanctuary.
67.26: The princes went first, next before the players on instruments, in the midst of damsels playing on timbrels.
67.27: Praise God in the congregations, the Lord from the fountains of Israel.
67.28: There is Benjamin the younger one in ecstasy, the princes of Juda their rulers, the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.
67.29: O God, command thou thy strength: strengthen, O God, this which thou hast wrought in us.
67.30: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents to thee.
67.31: Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed: let the crowd of bulls with the heifers of the nations be rebuked , so that they who have been proved with silver may not be shut out: scatter thou the nations that wish for wars.
67.32: Ambassadors shall arrive out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall hasten to stretch out her hand readily to God.
67.33: Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth; sing psalms to the Lord. Pause.
67.34: Sing to God that rides on the heaven of heaven, eastward: lo, he will utter a mighty sound with his voice.
67.35: Give ye glory to God: his excellency is over Israel, and his power is in the clouds.
67.36: God is wonderful in his holy places , the God of Israel: he will give power and strength to his people: blessed be God.

68.1: For the end, a Psalm of David, for alternate strains .
68.2: Save me, O God; for the waters have come in to my soul.
68.3: I am stuck fast in deep mire, and there is no standing: I am come in to the depths of the sea, and a storm has overwhelmed me.
68.4: I am weary of crying, my throat has become hoarse; mine eyes have failed by my waiting on my God.
68.5: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: my enemies that persecute me unrighteously are strengthened: then I restored that which I took not away.
68.6: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my transgressions are not hidden from thee.
68.7: Let not them that wait on thee, O Lord of hosts, be ashamed on my account: let not them that seek thee, be ashamed on my account, O God of Israel.
68.8: For I have suffered reproach for thy sake; shame has covered my face.
68.9: I became strange to my brethren, and a stranger to my mother's children.
68.10: For the zeal of thine house has eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
68.11: And I bowed down my soul with fasting, and that was made my reproach.
68.12: And I put on sackcloth for my covering; and I became a proverb to them.
68.13: They that sit in the gate talked against me, and they that drank wine sang against me.
68.14: But I will cry to thee, O Lord, in my prayer; O God, it is a propitious time: in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
68.15: Save me from the mire, that I stick not in it : let me be delivered from them that hate me, and from the deep waters.
68.16: Let not the waterflood drown me, nor let the deep swallow me up; neither let the well shut its mouth upon me.
68.17: Hear me, O Lord; for thy mercy is good: according to the multitude of thy compassions look upon me.
68.18: And turn not away thy face from thy servant; for I am afflicted: hear me speedily.
68.19: Draw nigh to my soul and redeem it: deliver me because of mine enemies.
68.20: For thou knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my confusion; all that afflict me are before thee.
68.21: My soul has waited for reproach and misery; and I waited for one to grieve with me, but there was none; and for one to comfort me, but I found none.
68.22: They gave me also gall for my food, and made me drink vinegar for my thirst.
68.23: Let their table before them be for a snare, and for a recompence, and for a stumbling-block.
68.24: Let their eyes be darkened that they should not see; and bow down their back continually.
68.25: Pour out thy wrath upon them, and let the fury of thine anger take hold on them.
68.26: Let their habitation be made desolate; and let there be no inhabitant in their tents:
68.27: because they persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; and they have added to the grief of my wounds.
68.28: Add iniquity to their iniquity; and let them not come into thy righteousness.
68.29: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous.
68.30: I am poor and sorrowful; but the salvation of thy countenance has helped me.
68.31: I will praise the name of my God with a song, I will magnify him with praise;
68.32: and this shall please God more than a young calf having horns and hoofs.
68.33: Let the poor see and rejoice; seek the Lord diligently, and ye shall live.
68.34: For the Lord hears the poor, and does not set at nought his fettered ones.
68.35: Let the heavens and the earth praise him, the sea, and all things moving in them.
68.36: For God will save Sion, and the cities of Judea shall be built; and men shall dwell there, and inherit it.
68.37: And the seed of his servants shall possess it, and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

69.1: For the end, by David for a remembrance, that the Lord may save me.
69.2: Draw nigh, O God, to my help.
69.3: Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek my soul: let them be turned backward and put to shame, that wish me evil.
69.4: Let them that say to me, Aha, aha, be turned back and put to shame immediately.
69.5: Let all that seek thee exult and be glad in thee: and let those that love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified.
69.6: But I am poor and needy; O God, help me: thou art my helper and deliverer, O Lord, delay not.

70.1: By David, a Psalm sung by the sons of Jonadab, and the first that were taken captive. O Lord, I have hoped in thee: let me never be put to shame.
70.2: In thy righteousness deliver me and rescue me: incline thine ear to me, and save me.
70.3: Be to me a protecting God, and a strong hold to save me: for thou art my fortress and my refuge.
70.4: Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the transgressor and unjust man.
70.5: For thou art my support, O Lord; O Lord, thou art my hope from my youth.
70.6: On thee have I been stayed from the womb: from the belly of my mother thou art my protector: of thee is my praise continually.
70.7: I am become as it were a wonder to many; but thou art my strong helper.
70.8: Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may hymn thy glory, and thy majesty all the day.
70.9: Cast me not off at the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength fails.
70.10: For mine enemies have spoken against me; and they that lay wait for my soul have taken counsel together,
70.11: saying, God has forsaken him: persecute ye and take him; for there is none to deliver him .
70.12: O God, go not far from me, O my God, draw nigh to my help.
70.13: Let those that plot against my soul be ashamed and utterly fail: let those that seek my hurt be clothed with shame and dishonour.
70.14: But I will hope continually, and will praise thee more and more.
70.15: My mouth shall declare thy righteousness openly, and thy salvation all the day; for I am not acquainted with the affairs of men .
70.16: I will go on in the might of the Lord: O Lord, I will make mention of thy righteousness only.
70.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth, and until now will I declare thy wonders;
70.18: even until I am old and advanced in years. O God, forsake me not; until I shall have declared thine arm to all the generation that is to come:
70.19: even thy power and thy righteousness, O God, up to the highest heavens, even the mighty works which thou hast done: O God, who is like to thee?
70.20: What afflictions many and sore hast thou shewed me! yet thou didst turn and quicken me, and broughtest me again from the depths of the earth.
70.21: Thou didst multiply thy righteousness, and didst turn and comfort me, and broughtest me again out of the depths of the earth.
70.22: I will also therefore give thanks to thee, O God, because of thy truth, on an instrument of psalmody: I will sing psalms to thee on the harp, O Holy One of Israel.
70.23: My lips shall rejoice when I sing to thee; and my soul, which thou hast redeemed.
70.24: Moreover also my tongue shall dwell all the day upon thy righteousness; when they shall be ashamed and confounded that seek my hurt.

71.1: For Solomon. O God, give thy judgment to the king, and thy righteousness to the king's son;
71.2: that he may judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.
71.3: Let the mountains and the hills raise peace to thy people:
71.4: he shall judge the poor of the people in righteousness, and save the children of the needy; and shall bring low the false accuser.
71.5: And he shall continue as long as the sun, and before the moon for ever.
71.6: He shall come down as rain upon a fleece; and as drops falling upon the earth.
71.7: In his days shall righteousness spring up; and abundance of peace till the moon be removed.
71.8: And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
71.9: The Ethiopians shall fall down before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.
71.10: The kings of Tharsis, and the isles, shall bring presents: the kings of the Arabians and Saba shall offer gifts.
71.11: And all kings shall worship him; all the Gentiles shall serve him.
71.12: For he has delivered the poor from the oppressor; and the needy who had no helper.
71.13: He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall deliver the souls of the needy.
71.14: He shall redeem their souls from usury and injustice: and their name shall be precious before him.
71.15: And he shall live, and there shall be given him of the gold of Arabia: and men shall pray for him continually; and all the day shall they praise him.
71.16: There shall be an establishment on the earth on the tops of the mountains: the fruit thereof shall be exalted above Libanus, and they of the city shall flourish as grass of the earth.
71.17: Let his name be blessed for ever: his name shall endure longer than the sun: and all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.
71.18: Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
71.19: And blessed is his glorious name for ever, even for ever and ever: and all the earth shall be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it.
71.20: The hymns of David the son of Jessæ are ended.

72.1: A Psalm for Asaph. How good is God to Israel, to the upright in heart!
72.2: But my feet were almost overthrown; my goings very nearly slipped.
72.3: For I was jealous of the transgressors, beholding the tranquillity of sinners.
72.4: For there is no sign of reluctance in their death: and they have firmness under their affliction.
72.5: They are not in the troubles of other men; and they shall not be scourged with other men.
72.6: Therefore pride has possessed them; they have clothed themselves with their injustice and ungodliness.
72.7: Their injustice shall go forth as out of fatness: they have fulfilled their intention.
72.8: They have taken counsel and spoken in wickedness: they have uttered unrighteousness loftily.
72.9: They have set their mouth against heaven, and their tongue has gone through upon the earth.
72.10: Therefore shall my people return hither: and full days shall be found with them.
72.11: And they said, How does God know? and is there knowledge in the Most High?
72.12: Behold, these are the sinners, and they that prosper always: they have possessed wealth.
72.13: And I said, Verily in vain have I justified my heart, and washed my hands in innocency.
72.14: For I was plagued all the day, and my reproof was every morning.
72.15: If I said, I will speak thus; behold, I should have broken covenant with the generation of thy children.
72.16: And I undertook to understand this, but it is too hard for me,
72.17: until I go into the sanctuary of God; and so understand the latter end.
72.18: Surely thou hast appointed judgments to them because of their crafty dealings: thou hast cast them down when they were lifted up.
72.19: How have they become desolate! suddenly they have failed: they have perished because of their iniquity.
72.20: As the dream of one awakening, O Lord, in thy city thou wilt despise their image.
72.21: For my heart has rejoiced, and my reins have been gladdened.
72.22: But I was vile and knew not: I became brutish before thee.
72.23: Yet I am continually with thee: thou hast holden my right hand.
72.24: Thou hast guided me by thy counsel, and thou hast taken me to thyself with glory.
72.25: For what have I in heaven but thee ? and what have I desired upon the earth beside thee?
72.26: My heart and my flesh have failed: but God is the strength of my heart, and God is my portion for ever.
72.27: For, behold, they that remove themselves far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed every one that goes a whoring from thee.
72.28: But it is good for me to cleave close to God, to put my trust in the Lord; that I may proclaim all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

73.1: A Psalm of instruction for Asaph. Wherefore hast thou rejected us , O God, for ever? wherefore is thy wrath kindled against the sheep of thy pasture?
73.2: Remember thy congregation which thou hast purchased from the beginning; thou didst ransom the rod of thine inheritance; this mount Sion wherein thou hast dwelt.
73.3: Lift up thine hands against their pride continually; because of all that the enemy has done wickedly in thy holy places.
73.4: And they that hate thee have boasted in the midst of thy feast; they have set up their standards for signs,
73.5: ignorantly as it were in the entrance above;
73.6: they cut down its doors at once with axes as in a wood of trees; they have broken it down with hatchet and stone cutter.
73.7: They have burnt thy sanctuary with fire to the ground; they have profaned the habitation of thy name.
73.8: They have said in their heart, even all their kindred together, Come, let us abolish the feasts of the Lord from the earth.
73.9: We have not seen our signs; there is no longer a prophet; and God will not know us any more.
73.10: How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach? shall the enemy provoke thy name for ever?
73.11: Wherefore turnest thou away thine hand, and thy right hand from the midst of thy bosom for ever?
73.12: But God is our King of old; he has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
73.13: Thou didst establish the sea, in thy might, thou didst break to pieces the heads of the dragons in the water.
73.14: Thou didst break to pieces the heads of the dragon; thou didst give him for meat to the Ethiopian nations.
73.15: Thou didst cleave fountains and torrents; thou driedst up mighty rivers.
73.16: The day is thine, and the night is thine; thou hast prepared the sun and the moon.
73.17: Thou hast made all the borders of the earth; thou hast made summer and spring.
73.18: Remember this thy creation: an enemy has reproached the Lord, and a foolish people has provoked thy name.
73.19: Deliver not to the wild beasts a soul that gives praise to thee: forget not for ever the souls of thy poor.
73.20: Look upon thy covenant: for the dark places of the earth are filled with the habitations of iniquity.
73.21: Let not the afflicted and shamed one be rejected: the poor and needy shall praise thy name.
73.22: Arise, O God, plead thy cause: remember thy reproaches that come from the foolish one all the day.
73.23: Forget not the voice of thy suppliants: let the pride of them that hate thee continually ascend before thee.

74.1: For the end, Destroy not, a Psalm of a Song for Asaph.
74.2: We will give thanks to thee, O God, we will give thanks, and call upon thy name: I will declare all thy wonderful works.
74.3: When I shall take a set time, I will judge righteously.
74.4: The earth is dissolved, and all that dwell in it: I have strengthened its pillars. Pause.
74.5: I said unto the transgressors, Do not transgress; and to the sinners, Lift not up the horn.
74.6: Lift not up your horn on high; speak not unrighteousness against God.
74.7: For good comes neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert mountains.
74.8: For God is the judge; he puts down one, and raises up another.
74.9: For there is a cup in the hand of the Lord, full of unmingled wine; and he has turned it from side to side, but its dregs have not been wholly poured out; all the sinners of the earth shall drink them .
74.10: But I will exult for ever: I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
74.11: And I will break all the horns of sinners; but the horns of the righteous one shall be exalted.

75.1: For the end, among the Hymns, a Psalm for Asaph; a Song for the Assyrian.
75.2: God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel.
75.3: And his place has been in peace, and his dwelling-place in Sion.
75.4: There he broke the power of the bows, the shield, and the sword, and the battle. Pause.
75.5: Thou dost wonderfully shine forth from the everlasting mountains.
75.6: All the simple ones in heart were troubled; all the men of wealth have slept their sleep, and have found nothing in their hands.
75.7: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, the riders on horses slumbered.
75.8: Thou art terrible; and who shall withstand thee, because of thine anger?
75.9: Thou didst cause judgment to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still,
75.10: when God arose to judgment, to save all the meek in heart. Pause.
75.11: For the inward thought of man shall give thanks to thee: and the memorial of his inward thought shall keep a feast to thee.
75.12: Vow, and pay your vows to the Lord our God; all that are round about him shall bring gifts, even to him that is terrible,
75.13: and that takes away the spirits of princes; to him that is terrible among the kings of the earth.

76.1: For the end, for Idithun, a Psalm of Asaph.
76.2: I cried to the Lord with my voice, yea, my voice was addressed to God; and he gave heed to me.
76.3: In the day of mine affliction I earnestly sought the Lord; even with my hands by night before him, and I was not deceived; my soul refused to be comforted.
76.4: I remembered God, and rejoiced; I poured out my complaint, and my soul fainted. Pause.
76.5: All mine enemies set a watch against me : I was troubled, and spoke not.
76.6: I considered the days of old, and remembered ancient years.
76.7: And I meditated; I communed with my heart by night, and diligently searched my spirit, saying ,
76.8: Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will he be well pleased no more?
76.9: Will he cut off his mercy for ever, even for ever and ever?
76.10: Will God forget to pity? or will he shut up his compassions in his wrath? Pause.
76.11: And I said, Now I have begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.
76.12: I remembered the works of the Lord; for I will remember thy wonders from the beginning.
76.13: And I will meditate on all thy works, and will consider thy doings.
76.14: O God, thy way is in the sanctuary; who is a great God as our God?
76.15: Thou art the God that doest wonders; thou hast made known thy power among the nations.
76.16: Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Pause.
76.17: The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee, and feared; and the depths were troubled.
76.18: There was an abundant sound of waters: the clouds uttered a voice; for thine arrows went abroad.
76.19: The voice of thy thunder was abroad, and around thy lightnings appeared to the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
76.20: Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters, and thy footsteps cannot be known.
76.21: Thou didst guide thy people as sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

77.1: A Psalm of instruction for Asaph. Give heed, O my people, to my law: incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
77.2: I will open my mouth in parables: I will utter dark sayings which have been from the beginning.
77.3: All which we have heard and known, and our fathers have declared to us.
77.4: They were not hid from their children to a second generation; the fathers declaring the praises of the Lord, and his mighty acts, and his wonders which he wrought.
77.5: And he raised up a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, to make it known to their children:
77.6: that another generation might know, even the sons which should be born; and they should arise and declare them to their children.
77.7: That they might set their hope on God, and not forget the works of God, but diligently seek his commandments.
77.8: That they should not be as their fathers, a perverse and provoking generation; a generation which set not its heart aright, and its spirit was not steadfast with God.
77.9: The children of Ephraim, bending and shooting with the bow, turned back in the day of battle.
77.10: They kept not the covenant of God, and would not walk in his law.
77.11: And they forgot his benefits, and his miracles which he had shewed them;
77.12: the miracles which he wrought before their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Tanes.
77.13: He clave the sea, and led them through: he made the waters to stand as in a bottle.
77.14: And he guided them with a cloud by day, and all the night with a light of fire.
77.15: He clave a rock in the wilderness, and made them drink as in a great deep.
77.16: And he brought water out of the rock, and caused waters to flow down as rivers.
77.17: And they sinned yet more against him; they provoked the Most High in the wilderness.
77.18: And they tempted God in their hearts, in asking meat for the desire of their souls.
77.19: They spoke also against God, and said, Will God be able to prepare a table in the wilderness?
77.20: Forasmuch as he smote the rock, and the waters flowed, and the torrents ran abundantly; will he be able also to give bread, or prepare a table for his people?
77.21: Therefore the Lord heard, and was provoked: and fire was kindled in Jacob, and wrath went up against Israel.
77.22: Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in his salvation.
77.23: Yet he commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven,
77.24: and rained upon them manna to eat, and gave them the bread of heaven.
77.25: Man ate angels' bread; he sent them provision to the full.
77.26: He removed the south wind from heaven; and by his might he brought in the south-west wind.
77.27: And he rained upon them flesh like dust, and feathered birds like the sand of the seas.
77.28: And they fell into the midst of their camp, round about their tents.
77.29: So they ate, and were completely filled; and he gave them their desire.
77.30: They were not disappointed of their desire: but when their food was yet in their mouth,
77.31: then the indignation of God rose up against them, and slew the fattest of them, and overthrew the choice men of Israel.
77.32: In the midst of all this they sinned yet more, and believed not his miracles.
77.33: And their days were consumed in vanity, and their years with anxiety.
77.34: When he slew them, they sought him: and they returned and called betimes upon God.
77.35: And they remembered that God was their helper, and the most high God was their redeemer.
77.36: Yet they loved him only with their mouth, and lied to him with their tongue.
77.37: For their heart was not right with him, neither were they steadfast in his covenant.
77.38: But he is compassionate, and will forgive their sins, and will not destroy them : yea, he will frequently turn away his wrath, and will not kindle all his anger.
77.39: And he remembered that they are flesh; a wind that passes away, and returns not.
77.40: How often did they provoke him in the wilderness, and anger him in a dry land!
77.41: Yea, they turned back, and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
77.42: They remembered not his hand, the day in which he delivered them from the hand of the oppressor.
77.43: How he had wrought his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Tanes:
77.44: and had changed their rivers into blood; and their streams, that they should not drink.
77.45: He sent against them the dog-fly, and it devoured them; and the frog, and it spoiled them.
77.46: And he gave their fruit to the canker worm, and their labours to the locust.
77.47: He killed their vines with hail, and their sycamores with frost.
77.48: And he gave up their cattle to hail, and their substance to the fire.
77.49: He sent out against them the fury of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and affliction, a message by evil angels.
77.50: He made a way for his wrath; he spared not their souls from death, but consigned their cattle to death;
77.51: and smote every first-born in the land of Egypt; the first-fruits of their labours in the tents of Cham.
77.52: And he removed his people like sheep; he led them as a flock in the wilderness.
77.53: And he guided them with hope, and they feared not: but the sea covered their enemies.
77.54: And he brought them in to the mountain of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand had purchased.
77.55: And he cast out the nations from before them, and made them to inherit by a line of inheritance, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
77.56: Yet they tempted and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies.
