118.118: Thou hast brought to nought all that depart from thine ordinances; for their inward thought is unrighteous.
118.119: I have reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore have I loved thy testimonies.
118.120: Penetrate my flesh with thy fear; for I am afraid of thy judgments.
118.121: I have done judgment and justice; deliver me not up to them that injure me.
118.122: Receive thy servant for good: let not the proud accuse me falsely.
118.123: Mine eyes have failed for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness.
118.124: Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy, and teach me thine ordinances.
118.125: I am thy servant; instruct me, and I shall know thy testimonies.
118.126: It is time for the Lord to work: they have utterly broken thy law.
118.127: Therefore have I loved thy commandments more than gold, or the topaz.
118.128: Therefore I directed myself according to all thy commandments: I have hated every unjust way.
118.129: Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore my soul has sought them out.
118.130: The manifestation of thy words will enlighten, and instruct the simple.
118.131: I opened my mouth, and drew breath: for I earnestly longed after thy commandments.
118.132: Look upon me and have mercy upon me, after the manner of them that love thy name.
118.133: Order my steps according to thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.
118.134: Deliver me from the false accusation of men: so will I keep thy commandments.
118.135: Cause thy face to shine upon thy servant: and teach me thine ordinances.
118.136: Mine eyes have been bathed in streams of water, because I kept not thy law.
118.137: Righteous art thou, O Lord, and upright are thy judgments.
118.138: Thou hast commanded righteousness and perfect truth, as thy testimonies.
118.139: Thy zeal has quite wasted me: because mine enemies have forgotten thy words.
118.140: Thy word has been very fully tried; and thy servant loves it.
118.141: I am young and despised: yet I have not forgotten thine ordinances.
118.142: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is truth.
118.143: Afflictions and distresses found me: but thy commandments were my meditation.
118.144: Thy testimonies are an everlasting righteousness: instruct me, and I shall live.
118.145: I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will search out thine ordinances.
118.146: I cried to thee; save me, and I will keep thy testimonies.
118.147: I arose before the dawn, and cried: I hoped in thy words.
118.148: Mine eyes prevented the dawn, that I might meditate on thine oracles.
118.149: Hear my voice, O Lord, according to thy mercy; quicken me according to thy judgment.
118.150: They have drawn nigh who persecuted me unlawfully; and they are far removed from thy law.
118.151: Thou art near, O Lord; and all thy ways are truth.
118.152: I have known of old concerning thy testimonies, that thou hast founded them for ever.
118.153: Look upon mine affliction, and rescue me; for I have not forgotten thy law.
118.154: Plead my cause, and ransom me: quicken me because of thy word.
118.155: Salvation is far from sinners: for they have not searched out thine ordinances.
118.156: Thy mercies, O Lord, are many: quicken me according to thy judgment.
118.157: Many are they that persecute me and oppress me: but I have not declined from thy testimonies.
118.158: I beheld men acting foolishly, and I pined away; for they kept not thine oracles.
118.159: Behold, I have loved thy commandments, O Lord: quicken me in thy mercy.
118.160: The beginning of thy words is truth; and all the judgments of thy righteousness endure for ever.
118.161: Princes persecuted me without a cause, but my heart feared because of thy words.
118.162: I will exult because of thine oracles, as one that finds much spoil.
118.163: I hate and abhor unrighteousness; but I love thy law.
118.164: Seven times in a day have I praised thee because of the judgments of thy righteousness.
118.165: Great peace have they that love thy law: and there is no stumbling-block to them.
118.166: I waited for thy salvation, O Lord, and have loved thy commandments.
118.167: My soul has kept thy testimonies, and loved them exceedingly.
118.168: I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies; for all my ways are before thee, O Lord.
118.169: Let my supplication come near before thee, O Lord; instruct me according to thine oracle.
118.170: Let my petition come in before thee, O Lord; deliver me according to thine oracle.
118.171: Let my lips utter a hymn, when thou shalt have taught me thine ordinances.
118.172: Let my tongue utter thine oracles; for all thy commandments are righteous.
118.173: Let thine hand be prompt to save me; for I have chosen thy commandments.
118.174: I have longed after thy salvation, O Lord; and thy law is my meditation.
118.175: My soul shall live, and shall praise thee; and thy judgments shall help me.
118.176: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I have not forgotten thy commandments.

119.1: A Song of Degrees. In mine affliction I cried to the Lord, and he hearkened to me.
119.2: Deliver my soul, O Lord, from unjust lips, and from a deceitful tongue.
119.3: What should be given to thee, and what should be added to thee, for thy crafty tongue?
119.4: Sharpened weapons of the mighty, with coals of the desert.
119.5: Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged; I have tabernacled among the tents of Kedar.
119.6: My soul has long been a sojourner;
119.7: I was peaceable among them that hated peace; when I spoke to them, they warred against me without a cause.

120.1: A Song of Degrees. I lifted up mine eyes to the mountains, whence my help shall come.
120.2: My help shall come from the Lord, who made the heaven and the earth.
120.3: Let not thy foot be moved; and let not thy keeper slumber.
120.4: Behold, he that keeps Israel shall not slumber nor sleep.
120.5: The Lord shall keep thee: the Lord is thy shelter upon thy right hand.
120.6: The sun shall not burn thee by day, neither the moon by night.
120.7: May the Lord preserve thee from all evil: the Lord shall keep thy soul.
120.8: The Lord shall keep thy coming in, and thy going out, from henceforth and even for ever.

121.1: A Song of Degrees. I was glad when they said to me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.
121.2: Our feet stood in thy courts, O Jerusalem.
121.3: Jerusalem is built as a city whose fellowship is complete.
121.4: For thither the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.
121.5: For there are set thrones for judgment, even thrones for the house of David.
121.6: Pray now for the peace of Jerusalem: and let there be prosperity to them that love thee.
121.7: Let peace, I pray, be within thine host, and prosperity in thy palaces.
121.8: For the sake of my brethren and my neighbours, I have indeed spoken peace concerning thee.
121.9: Because of the house of the Lord our God, I have diligently sought thy good.

122.1: A Song of Degrees. Unto thee who dwellest in heaven have I lifted up mine eyes.
122.2: Behold, as the eyes of servants are directed to the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maid-servant to the hands of her mistress; so our eyes are directed to the Lord our God, until he have mercy upon us.
122.3: Have pity upon us, O Lord, have pity upon us: for we are exceedingly filled with contempt.
122.4: Yea , our soul has been exceedingly filled with it : let the reproach be to them that are at ease, and contempt to the proud.

123.1: A Song of Degrees. If it had not been that the Lord was among us, let Israel now say;
123.2: if it had not been that the Lord was among us, when men rose up against us;
123.3: verily they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us:
123.4: verily the water would have drowned us, our soul would have gone under the torrent.
123.5: Yea, our soul would have gone under the overwhelming water.
123.6: Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us for a prey to their teeth.
123.7: Our soul has been delivered as a sparrow from the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are delivered.
123.8: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

124.1: A Song of Degrees. They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: he that dwells in Jerusalem shall never be moved.
124.2: The mountains are round about her, and so the Lord is round about his people, from henceforth and even for ever.
124.3: For the Lord will not allow the rod of sinners to be upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous should stretch forth their hands to iniquity.
124.4: Do good, O Lord, to them that are good, and to them that are upright in heart.
124.5: But them that turn aside to crooked ways the Lord will lead away with the workers of iniquity: but peace shall be upon Israel.

125.1: A Song of Degrees. When the Lord turned the captivity of Sion, we became as comforted ones.
125.2: Then was our mouth filled with joy, and our tongue with exultation: then would they say among the Gentiles,
125.3: The Lord has done great things among them. The Lord has done great things for us, we became joyful.
125.4: Turn, O Lord, our captivity, as the streams in the south.
125.5: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
125.6: They went on and wept as they cast their seeds; but they shall surely come with exultation, bringing their sheaves with them .

126.1: A Song of Degrees. Except the Lord build the house, they that build labour in vain: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman watches in vain.
126.2: It is vain for you to rise early: ye rise up after resting, ye that eat the bread of grief; while he gives sleep to his beloved.
126.3: Behold, the inheritance of the Lord, children, the reward of the fruit of the womb.
126.4: As arrows in the hand of a mighty man; so are the children of those who were outcasts.
126.5: Blessed is the man who shall satisfy his desire with them: they shall not be ashamed when they shall speak to their enemies in the gates.

127.1: A Song of Degrees. Blessed are all they that fear the Lord; who walk in his ways.
127.2: Thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.
127.3: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine on the sides of thy house: thy children as young olive-plants round about thy table.
127.4: Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that fears the Lord.
127.5: May the Lord bless thee out of Sion; and mayest thou see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.
127.6: And mayest thou see thy children's children. Peace be upon Israel.

128.1: A Song of Degrees. Many a time have they warred against me from my youth, let Israel now say:
128.2: Many a time have they warred against me from my youth: and yet they prevailed not against me.
128.3: The sinners wrought upon my back: they prolonged their iniquity.
128.4: The righteous Lord has cut asunder the necks of sinners.
128.5: Let all that hate Sion be put to shame and turned back.
128.6: Let them be as the grass of the house-tops, which withers before it is plucked up.
128.7: Wherewith the reaper fills not his hand, nor he that makes up the sheaves, his bosom.
128.8: Neither do they that go by say, The blessing of the Lord be upon you: we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.

129.1: A Song of Degrees. Out of the depths have I cried to thee, O Lord.
129.2: O Lord, hearken to my voice; let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication.
129.3: If thou, O Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?
129.4: For with thee is forgiveness: for thy name's sake
129.5: have I waited for thee, O Lord, my soul has waited for thy word.
129.6: My soul has hoped in the Lord; from the morning watch till night.
129.7: Let Israel hope in the Lord: for with the Lord is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.
129.8: And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

130.1: A Song of Degrees. O Lord, my heart is not exalted, neither have mine eyes been haughtily raised: neither have I exercised myself in great matters , nor in things too wonderful for me.
130.2: I shall have sinned if I have not been humble, but have exalted my soul: according to the relation of a weaned child to his mother, so wilt thou recompense my soul.
130.3: Let Israel hope in the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.

131.1: A Song of Degrees. Lord, remember David, and all his meekness:
131.2: how he sware to the Lord, and vowed to the God of Jacob, saying ,
131.3: I will not go into the tabernacle of my house; I will not go up to the couch of my bed;
131.4: I will not give sleep to mine eyes, nor slumber to mine eyelids, nor rest to my temples,
131.5: until I find a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
131.6: Behold, we heard of it in Ephratha; we found it in the fields of the wood.
131.7: Let us enter into his tabernacles: let us worship at the place where his feet stood.
131.8: Arise, O Lord, into thy rest; thou, and the ark of thine holiness.
131.9: Thy priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness; and thy saints shall exult.
131.10: For the sake of thy servant David turn not away the face of thine anointed.
131.11: The Lord sware in truth to David, and he will not annul it, saying , Of the fruit of thy body will I set a king upon thy throne.
131.12: If thy children will keep my covenant, and these my testimonies which I shall teach them, their children also shall sit upon thy throne for ever.
131.13: For the Lord has elected Sion, he has chosen her for a habitation for himself, saying ,
131.14: This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have chosen it.
131.15: I will surely bless her provision: I will satisfy her poor with bread.
131.16: I will clothe her priests with salvation; and her saints shall greatly exult.
131.17: There will I cause to spring up a horn to David: I have prepared a lamp for mine anointed.
131.18: His enemies will I clothe with shame; but upon himself shall my holiness flourish.

132.1: A Song of Degrees. See now! what is so good, or what so pleasant, as for brethren to dwell together?
132.2: It is as ointment on the head, that ran down to the beard, even the beard of Aaron; that ran down to the fringe of his clothing.
132.3: As the dew of Aermon, that comes down on the mountains of Sion: for there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for ever.

133.1: A Song of Degrees. Behold now, bless ye the Lord, all the servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.
133.2: Lift up your hands by night in the sanctuaries, and bless the Lord.
133.3: May the Lord, who made heaven and earth, bless thee out of Sion.

134.1: Alleluia. Praise ye the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, ye his servants,
134.2: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.
134.3: Praise ye the Lord; for the Lord is good: sing praises to his name; for it is good.
134.4: For the Lord has chosen Jacob for himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure.
134.5: For I know that the Lord is great, and our Lord is above all gods;
134.6: all that the Lord willed, he did in heaven, and on the earth, in the sea, and in all deeps.
134.7: Who brings up clouds from the extremity of the earth: he has made lightnings for the rain: he brings winds out of his treasures.
134.8: Who smote the first-born of Egypt, both of man and beast.
134.9: He sent signs and wonders into the midst of thee, O Egypt, on Pharao, and on all his servants.
134.10: Who smote many nations, and slew mighty kings;
134.11: Seon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Basan, and all the kingdoms of Chanaan:
134.12: and gave their land for an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel his people.
134.13: O Lord, thy name endures for ever, and thy memorial to all generations.
134.14: For the Lord shall judge his people, and comfort himself concerning his servants.
134.15: The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the works of men's hands.
134.16: They have a mouth, but they cannot speak; they have eyes, but they cannot see;
134.17: they have ears, but they cannot hear; for there is no breath in their mouth.
134.18: Let those who make them be made like to them; and all those who trust in them.
134.19: O house of Israel, bless ye the Lord: O house of Aaron, bless ye the Lord:
134.20: O house of Levi, bless ye the Lord: ye that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.
134.21: Blessed in Sion be the Lord, who dwells in Jerusalem.

135.1: Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord: for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.2: Give thanks to the God of gods: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.3: Give thanks to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.4: To him who alone has wrought great wonders: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.5: To him who made the heavens by understanding; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.6: To him who established the earth on the waters; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.7: To him who alone made great lights; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.8: The sun to rule the day; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.9: The moon and the stars to rule the night; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.10: To him who smote Egypt with their first-born; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.11: And brought Israel out of the midst of them; for his mercy endures for ever:
135.12: with a strong hand, and a high arm: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.13: To him who divided the Red Sea into parts: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.14: and brought Israel through the midst of it: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.15: and overthrew Pharao and his host in the Red Sea: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.16: To him who led his people through the wilderness: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.17: To him who smote great kings: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.18: and slew mighty kings; for his mercy endures for ever:
135.19: Seon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.20: and Og king of Basan: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.21: and gave their land for an inheritance: for his mercy endures for ever:
135.22: even an inheritance to Israel his servant: for his mercy endures for ever.
135.23: For the Lord remembered us in our low estate; for his mercy endures for ever:
135.24: and redeemed us from our enemies; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.25: Who gives food to all flesh; for his mercy endures for ever.
135.26: Give thanks to the God of heaven; for his mercy endures for ever.

136.1: For David, a Psalm of Jeremias. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat; and wept when we remembered Sion.
136.2: We hung our harps on the willows in the midst of it.
136.3: For there they that had taken us captive asked of us the words of a song; and they that had carried us away asked a hymn, saying , Sing us one of the songs of Sion.
136.4: How should we sing the Lord's song in a strange land?
136.5: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill .
136.6: May my tongue cleave to my throat, if I do not remember thee; if I do not prefer Jerusalem as the chief of my joy.
136.7: Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it , rase it , even to its foundations.
136.8: Wretched daughter of Babylon! blessed shall he be who shall reward thee as thou hast rewarded us.
136.9: Blessed shall he be who shall seize and dash thine infants against the rock.

137.1: A Psalm for David, of Aggæus and Zacharias. I will give thee thanks, O Lord, with my whole heart; and I will sing psalms to thee before the angels; for thou hast heard all the words of my mouth.
137.2: I will worship toward thy holy temple, and give thanks to thy name, on account of thy mercy and thy truth; for thou hast magnified thy holy name above every thing.
137.3: In whatsoever day I shall call upon thee, hear me speedily; thou shalt abundantly provide me with thy power in my soul.
137.4: Let all the kings of the earth, O Lord, give thanks unto thee; for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.
137.5: And let them sing in the ways of the Lord; for great is the glory of the Lord.
137.6: For the Lord is high, and yet regards the lowly; and he knows high things from afar off.
137.7: Though I should walk in the midst of affliction, thou wilt quicken me; thou hast stretched forth thine hands against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand has saved me.
137.8: O Lord, thou shalt recompense them on my behalf: thy mercy, O Lord, endures for ever: overlook not the works of thine hands.

138.1: For the end, a Psalm of David. O Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me.
138.2: Thou knowest my down-sitting and mine up-rising: thou understandest my thoughts long before.
138.3: Thou hast traced my path and my bed, and hast foreseen all my ways.
138.4: For there is no unrighteous word in my tongue: behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things,
138.5: the last and the first: thou hast fashioned me, and laid thine hand upon me.
138.6: The knowledge of thee is too wonderful for me; it is very difficult, I cannot attain to it.
138.7: Whither shall I go from thy Spirit? and whither shall I flee from thy presence?
138.8: If I should go up to heaven, thou art there: if I should go down to hell, thou art present.
138.9: If I should spread my wings to fly straight forward, and sojourn at the extremity of the sea, it would be vain ,
138.10: for even there thy hand would guide me, and thy right hand would hold me.
138.11: When I said, Surely the darkness will cover me; even the night was light in my luxury.
138.12: For darkness will not be darkness with thee; but night will be light as day: as its darkness, so shall its light be to thee .
138.13: For thou, O Lord, hast possessed my reins; thou hast helped me from my mother's womb.
138.14: I will give thee thanks; for thou art fearfully wondrous; wondrous are thy works; and my soul knows it well.
138.15: My bones which thou madest in secret were not hidden from thee, nor my substance, in the lowest parts of the earth.
138.16: Thine eyes saw my unwrought substance , and all men shall be written in thy book; they shall be formed by day, though there should for a time be no one among them.
138.17: But thy friends, O God, have been greatly honoured by me; their rule has been greatly strengthened.
138.18: I will number them, and they shall be multiplied beyond the sand; I awake, and am still with thee.
138.19: Oh that thou wouldest slay the wicked, O God; depart from me, ye men of blood.
138.20: For thou wilt say concerning their thought, that they shall take thy cities in vain.
138.21: Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hate thee? and wasted away because of thine enemies?
138.22: I have hated them with perfect hatred; they were counted my enemies.
138.23: Prove me, O God, and know my heart; examine me, and know my paths;
138.24: and see if there is any way of iniquity in me, and lead me in an everlasting way.

139.1: For the end, a Psalm of David.
139.2: Rescue me, O Lord, from the evil man; deliver me from the unjust man.
139.3: Who have devised injustice in their hearts; all the day they prepared war.
139.4: They have sharpened their tongue as the tongue of a serpent; the poison of asps is under their lips. Pause.
139.5: Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner; rescue me from unjust men; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.
139.6: The proud have hid a snare for me, and have stretched out ropes for snares for my feet; they set a stumbling-block for me near the path. Pause.
139.7: I said to the Lord, Thou art my God; hearken, O Lord, to the voice of my supplication.
139.8: O Lord God, the strength of my salvation; thou hast screened my head in the day of battle.
139.9: Deliver me not, O Lord, to the sinner, according to my desire: they have devised mischief against me; forsake me not, lest they should be exalted. Pause.
139.10: As for the head of them that compass me, the mischief of their lips shall cover them.
139.11: Coals of fire shall fall upon them on the earth; and thou shalt cast them down in afflictions: they shall not bear up under them .
139.12: A talkative man shall not prosper on the earth: evils shall hunt the unrighteous man to destruction.
139.13: I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the poor, and the right of the needy ones.
139.14: Surely the righteous shall give thanks to thy name: the upright shall dwell in thy presence.

140.1: A Psalm of David. O Lord, I have cried to thee; hear me: attend to the voice of my supplication, when I cry to thee.
140.2: Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
140.3: Set a watch, O Lord, on my mouth, and a strong door about my lips.
140.4: Incline not my heart to evil things, to employ pretexts for sins, with men who work iniquity: and let me not unite with their choice ones.
140.5: The righteous shall chasten me with mercy, and reprove me: but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head: for yet shall my prayer also be in their pleasures.
140.6: Their mighty ones have been swallowed up near the rock: they shall hear my words, for they are sweet.
140.7: As a lump of earth is crushed upon the ground, our bones have been scattered by the mouth of the grave.
140.8: For mine eyes are to thee, O Lord God: I have hoped in thee; take not away my life.
140.9: Keep me from the snare which they have set for me, and from the stumbling-blocks of them that work iniquity.
140.10: Sinners shall fall by their own net: I am alone until I shall escape.

141.1: A Psalm of instruction for David, when he was in the cave,—a Prayer.
141.2: I cried to the Lord with my voice; with my voice I made supplication to the Lord.
141.3: I will pour out before him my supplication: I will declare before him mine affliction.
141.4: When my spirit was fainting within me, then thou knewest my paths; in the very way wherein I was walking, they hid a snare for me.
141.5: I looked on my right hand, and behold, for there was none that noticed me; refuge failed me; and there was none that cared for my soul.
141.6: I cried unto thee, O Lord, and said, Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living.
141.7: Attend to my supplication, for I am brought very low; deliver me from them that persecute me; for they are stronger than I.
141.8: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to thy name, O Lord; the righteous shall wait for me, until thou recompense me.

142.1: A Psalm of David, when his son pursued him. O Lord, attend to my prayer: hearken to my supplication in thy truth; hear me in thy righteousness.
142.2: And enter not into judgment with thy servant, for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.
142.3: For the enemy has persecuted my soul; he has brought my life down to the ground; he has made me to dwell in a dark place , as those that have been long dead.
142.4: Therefore my spirit was grieved in me; my heart was troubled within me.
142.5: I remembered the days of old; and I meditated on all thy doings: yea , I meditated on the works of thine hands.
142.6: I spread forth my hands to thee; my soul thirsts for thee, as a dry land. Pause.
142.7: Hear me speedily, O Lord; my spirit has failed; turn not away thy face from me, else I shall be like to them that go down to the pit.
142.8: Cause me to hear thy mercy in the morning; for I have hoped in thee; make known to me, O Lord, the way wherein I should walk; for I have lifted up my soul to thee.
142.9: Deliver me from mine enemies, O Lord; for I have fled to thee for refuge.
142.10: Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God; thy good Spirit shall guide me in the straight way .
142.11: Thou shalt quicken me, O Lord, for thy name's sake; in thy righteousness thou shalt bring my soul out of affliction.
142.12: And in thy mercy thou wilt destroy mine enemies, and wilt destroy all those that afflict my soul; for I am thy servant.

143.1: A Psalm of David concerning Goliad. Blessed be the Lord my God, who instructs my hands for battle, and my fingers for war.
143.2: My mercy, and my refuge; my helper, and my deliverer; my protector, in whom I have trusted; who subdues my people under me.
143.3: Lord, what is man, that thou art made known to him? or the son of man, that thou takest account of him?
143.4: Man is like to vanity: his days pass as a shadow.
143.5: O Lord, bow thy heavens, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.
143.6: Send lightning, and thou shalt scatter them: send forth thine arrows, and thou shalt discomfit them.
143.7: Send forth thine hand from on high; rescue me, and deliver me out of great waters, out of the hand of strange children;
143.8: whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity.
143.9: O God, I will sing a new song to thee: I will play to thee on a psaltery of ten strings.
143.10: Even to him who gives salvation to kings: who redeems his servant David from the hurtful sword.
143.11: Deliver me, and rescue me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity;
143.12: whose children are as plants, strengthened in their youth: their daughters are beautiful, sumptuously adorned after the similitude of a temple.
143.13: Their garners are full, and bursting with one kind of store after another; their sheep are prolific, multiplying in their streets.
143.14: Their oxen are fat: there is no falling down of a hedge, nor going out, nor cry in their folds.
143.15: Men bless the people to whom this lot belongs, but blessed is the people whose God is the Lord.

144.1: David's Psalm of praise. I will exalt thee, my God, my king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.
144.2: Every day will I bless thee, and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.
144.3: The Lord is great, and greatly to be praised; and there is no end of his greatness.
144.4: Generation after generation shall praise thy works, and tell of thy power.
144.5: And they shall speak of the glorious majesty of thy holiness, and recount thy wonders.
144.6: And they shall speak of the power of thy terrible acts ; and recount thy greatness.
144.7: They shall utter the memory of the abundance of thy goodness, and shall exult in thy righteousness.
144.8: The Lord is compassionate, and merciful; long-suffering, and abundant in mercy.
144.9: The Lord is good to those that wait on him ; and his compassions are over all his works.
144.10: Let all thy works, O Lord, give thanks to thee; and let thy saints bless thee.
144.11: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy dominion;
144.12: to make known to the sons of men thy power, and the glorious majesty of thy kingdom.
144.13: The Lord is faithful in his words, and holy in all his works.
144.14: The Lord supports all that are falling, and sets up all that are broken down.
144.15: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their food in due season.
144.16: Thou openest thine hands, and fillest every living thing with pleasure.
144.17: The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.
144.18: The Lord is near to all that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
144.19: He will perform the desire of them that fear him: and he will hear their supplication, and save them.
144.20: The Lord preserves all that love him: but all sinners he will utterly destroy.
144.21: My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever.

145.1: Alleluia, a Psalm of Aggæus and Zacharias. My soul, praise the Lord.
145.2: While I live will I praise the Lord: I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist.
145.3: Trust not in princes, nor in the children of men, in whom there is no safety.
145.4: His breath shall go forth, and he shall return to his earth; in that day all his thoughts shall perish.
145.5: Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God:
145.6: who made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all things in them: who keeps truth for ever:
145.7: who executes judgment for the wronged: who gives food to the hungry. The Lord looses the fettered ones:
145.8: the Lord gives wisdom to the blind: The Lord sets up the broken down: the Lord loves the righteous: the Lord preserves the strangers;
145.9: he will relieve the orphan and widow: but will utterly remove the way of sinners.
145.10: The Lord shall reign for ever, even thy God, O Sion, to all generations.

146.1: Alleluia, a Psalm of Aggæus and Zacharias. Praise ye the Lord: for psalmody is a good thing; let praise be sweetly sung to our God.
146.2: The Lord builds up Jerusalem; and he will gather together the dispersed of Israel.
146.3: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
146.4: He numbers the multitudes of stars; and calls them all by names.
146.5: Great is our Lord, and great is his strength; and his understanding is infinite.
146.6: The Lord lifts up the meek; but brings sinners down to the ground.
146.7: Begin the song with thanksgiving to the Lord; sing praises on the harp to our God:
146.8: who covers the heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who causes grass to spring up on the mountains, [and green herb for the service of men;]
146.9: and gives to cattle their food, and to the young ravens that call upon him.
146.10: He will not take pleasure in the strength of a horse; neither is he well-pleased with the legs of a man.
146.11: The Lord takes pleasure in them that fear him, and in all that hope in his mercy.

147.1: Alleluia, a Psalm of Aggæus and Zacharias. Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Sion.
147.2: For he has strengthened the bars of thy gates; he has blessed thy children within thee.
147.3: He makes thy borders peaceful, and fills thee with the flour of wheat.
147.4: He sends his oracle to the earth: his word will run swiftly.
147.5: He gives snow like wool: he scatters the mist like ashes.
147.6: Casting forth his ice like morsels: who shall stand before his cold?
147.7: He shall send out his word, and melt them: he shall blow with his wind, and the waters shall flow.
147.8: He sends his word to Jacob, his ordinances and judgments to Israel.
147.9: He has not done so to any other nation; and he has not shewn them his judgments.

148.1: Alleluia, a Psalm of Aggæus and Zacharias. Praise ye the Lord from the heavens: praise him in the highest.
148.2: Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts.
148.3: Praise him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars and light.
148.4: Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and the water that is above the heavens.
148.5: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created.
148.6: He has established them for ever, even for ever and ever: he has made an ordinance, and it shall not pass away.
148.7: Praise the Lord from the earth, ye serpents, and all deeps.
148.8: Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy wind; the things that perform his word.
148.9: Mountains, and all hills; fruitful trees, and all cedars:
148.10: wild beasts, and all cattle; reptiles, and winged birds:
148.11: kings of the earth, and all peoples; princes, and all judges of the earth:
148.12: young men and virgins, old men with youths:
148.13: let them praise the name of the Lord: for his name only is exalted; his praise is above the earth and heaven,
148.14: and he shall exalt the horn of his people, there is a hymn for all his saints, even of the children of Israel, a people who draw near to him.

149.1: Alleluia. Sing to the Lord a new song: his praise is in the assembly of the saints.
149.2: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him; and let the children of Sion exult in their king.
149.3: Let them praise his name in the dance: let them sing praises to him with timbrel and psaltery.
149.4: For the Lord takes pleasure in his people; and will exalt the meek with salvation.
149.5: The saints shall rejoice in glory; and shall exult on their beds.
149.6: The high praises of God shall be in their throat, and two-edged swords in their hands;
149.7: to execute vengeance on the nations, and punishments among the peoples;
149.8: to bind their kings with fetters, and their nobles with manacles of iron;
149.9: to execute on them the judgment written: this honour have all his saints.

150.1: Alleluia. Praise God in his holy places: praise him in the firmament of his power.
150.2: Praise him on account of his mighty acts: praise him according to his abundant greatness.
150.3: Praise him with the sound of a trumpet: praise him with psaltery and harp.
150.4: Praise him with timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and the organ.
150.5: Praise him with melodious cymbals: praise him with loud cymbals.
150.6: Let every thing that has breath praise the Lord.

151.1: This Psalm is a genuine one of David, though supernumerary, composed when he fought in single combat with Goliad. I was small among my brethren, and youngest in my father's house: I tended my father's sheep.
151.2: My hands formed a musical instrument, and my fingers tuned a psaltery.
151.3: And who shall tell my Lord? the Lord himself, he himself hears.
151.4: He sent forth his angel, and took me from my father's sheep, and he anointed me with the oil of his anointing.
151.5: My brothers were handsome and tall; but the Lord did not take pleasure in them.
151.6: I went forth to meet the Philistine; and he cursed me by his idols.
151.7: But I drew his own sword, and beheaded him, and removed reproach from the children of Israel.

1.1: The Proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel;
1.2: to know wisdom and instruction, and to perceive words of understanding;
1.3: to receive also hard sayings, and to understand true justice, and how to direct judgment;
1.4: that he might give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man discernment and understanding.
1.5: For by the hearing of these a wise man will be wiser, and the man of understanding will gain direction;
1.6: and will understand a parable, and a dark speech; the sayings of the wise also, and riddles.
1.7: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; and there is good understanding to all that practise it: and piety toward God is the beginning of discernment; but the ungodly will set at nought wisdom and instruction.
1.8: Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, and reject not the rules of thy mother.
1.9: For thou shalt receive for thine head a crown of graces, and a chain of gold round thy neck.
1.10: My son, let not ungodly men lead thee astray, neither consent thou to them .
1.11: If they should exhort thee, saying, Come with us, partake in blood, and let us unjustly hide the just man in the earth:
1.12: and let us swallow him alive, as Hades would , and remove the memorial of him from the earth:
1.13: let us seize on his valuable property, and let us fill our houses with spoils:
1.14: but do thou cast in thy lot with us, and let us all provide a common purse, and let us have one pouch:
1.15: go not in the way with them, but turn aside thy foot from their paths:
1.17: for nets are not without cause spread for birds.
1.18: For they that are concerned in murder store up evils for themselves; and the overthrow of transgressors is evil.
1.19: These are the ways of all that perform lawless deeds; for by ungodliness they destroy their own life.
1.20: Wisdom sings aloud in passages, and in the broad places speaks boldly.
1.21: And she makes proclamation on the top of the walls, and sits by the gates of princes; and at the gates of the city boldly says,
1.22: So long as the simple cleave to justice, they shall not be ashamed: but the foolish being lovers of haughtiness, having become ungodly have hated knowledge, and are become subject to reproofs.
1.23: Behold, I will bring forth to you the utterance of my breath, and I will instruct you in my speech.
1.24: Since I called, and ye did not hearken; and I spoke at length, and ye gave no heed;
1.25: but ye set at nought my counsels, and disregarded my reproofs;
1.26: therefore I also will laugh at your destruction; and I will rejoice against you when ruin comes upon you:
1.27: yea when dismay suddenly comes upon you, and your overthrow shall arrive like a tempest; and when tribulation and distress shall come upon you, or when ruin shall come upon you.
1.28: For it shall be that when ye call upon me, I will not hearken to you: wicked men shall seek me, but shall not find me .
1.29: For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the word of the Lord:
1.30: neither would they attend to my counsels, but derided my reproofs.
1.31: Therefore shall they eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own ungodliness.
1.32: For because they wronged the simple, they shall be slain; and an inquisition shall ruin the ungodly.
1.33: But he that hearkens to me shall dwell in confidence, and shall rest securely from all evil.

2.1: My son, if thou wilt receive the utterance of my commandment, and hide it with thee;
2.2: thine ear shall hearken to wisdom; thou shalt also apply thine heart to understanding, and shalt apply it to the instruction of thy son.
2.3: For if thou shalt call to wisdom, and utter thy voice for understanding;
2.4: and if thou shalt seek it as silver, and search diligently for it as for treasures;
2.5: then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.
2.6: For the Lord gives wisdom; and from his presence come knowledge and understanding,
2.7: and he treasures up salvation for them that walk uprightly: he will protect their way;
2.8: that he may guard the righteous ways: and he will preserve the way of them that fear him.
2.9: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment; and shalt direct all thy course aright.
2.10: For if wisdom shall come into thine understanding, and discernment shall seem pleasing to thy soul,
2.11: good counsel shall guard thee, and holy understanding shall keep thee;
2.12: to deliver thee from the evil way, and from the man that speaks nothing faithfully.
2.13: Alas for those who forsake right paths, to walk in ways of darkness;
2.14: who rejoice in evils, and delight in wicked perverseness;
2.15: whose paths are crooked, and their courses winding;
2.16: to remove thee far from the straight way, and to estrange thee from a righteous purpose. My son, let not evil counsel overtake thee,
2.17: of her who has forsaken the instruction of her youth, and forgotten the covenant of God.
2.18: For she has fixed her house near death, and guided her wheels near Hades with the giants.
2.19: None that go by her shall return, neither shall they take hold of right paths, for they are not apprehended of the years of life.
2.20: For had they gone in good paths, they would have found the paths of righteousness easy.
2.21: For the upright shall dwell in the earth, and the holy shall be left behind in it.
2.22: The paths of the ungodly shall perish out of the earth, and transgressors shall be driven away from it.

3.1: My son, forget not my laws; but let thine heart keep my words:
3.2: for length of existence, and years of life, and peace, shall they add to thee.
3.3: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee; but bind them about thy neck:
3.4: so shalt thou find favour: and do thou provide things honest in the sight of the Lord, and of men.
3.5: Trust in God with all thine heart; and be not exalted in thine own wisdom.
3.6: In all thy ways acquaint thyself with her, that she may rightly direct thy paths.
3.7: Be not wise in thine own conceit; but fear God, and depart from all evil.
3.8: Then shall there be health to thy body, and good keeping to thy bones.
3.9: Honour the Lord with thy just labours, and give him the first of thy fruits of righteousness:
3.10: that thy storehouses may be completely filled with corn, and that thy presses may burst forth with wine.
3.11: My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
3.12: for whom the Lord loves, he rebukes, and scourges every son whom he receives.
3.13: Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who knows prudence.
3.14: For it is better to traffic for her, than for treasures of gold and silver.
3.15: And she is more valuable than precious stones: no evil thing shall resist her: she is well known to all that approach her, and no precious thing is equal to her in value.
3.16: out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and she carries law and mercy upon her tongue.
3.17: Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are peaceful.
3.18: She is a tree of life to all that lay hold upon her; and she is a secure help to all that stay themselves on her, as on the Lord.
3.19: God by wisdom founded the earth, and by prudence he prepared the heavens.
3.20: By understanding were the depths broken up, and the clouds dropped water.
3.21: My son, let them not pass from thee , but keep my counsel and understanding:
3.22: and it shall be health to thy flesh, and safety to thy bones:
3.23: that thou mayest go confidently in peace in all thy ways, and that thy foot may not stumble.
3.24: For if thou rest, thou shalt be undismayed; and if thou sleep, thou shalt slumber sweetly.
3.25: And thou shalt not be afraid of alarm coming upon thee, neither of approaching attacks of ungodly men.
3.26: For the Lord shall be over all thy ways, and shall establish thy foot that thou be not moved.
3.27: Forbear not to do good to the poor, whensoever thy hand may have power to help him .
3.28: Say not, Come back another time, to-morrow I will give; while thou art able to do him good: for thou knowest not what the next day will bring forth.
3.29: Devise not evil against thy friend, living near thee and trusting in thee.
3.30: Be not ready to quarrel with a man without a cause, lest he do thee some harm.
3.31: Procure not the reproaches of bad men, neither do thou covet their ways.
3.32: For every transgressor is unclean before the Lord; neither does he sit among the righteous.
3.33: The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly; but the habitations of the just are blessed.
3.34: The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble.
3.35: The wise shall inherit glory; but the ungodly have exalted their own dishonour.

4.1: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.
4.2: For I give you a good gift; forsake ye not my law.
4.3: For I also was a son obedient to my father, and loved in the sight of my mother:
4.4: who spoke and instructed me, saying , Let our speech be fixed in thine heart, keep our commandments, forget them not:
4.5: and do not neglect the speech of my mouth.
4.6: And forsake it not, and it shall cleave to thee: love it, and it shall keep thee.
4.8: Secure it, and it shall exalt thee: honour it, that it may embrace thee;
4.9: that it may give unto thy head a crown of graces, and may cover thee with a crown of delight.
4.10: Hear, my son, and receive my words; and the years of thy life shall be increased, that the resources of thy life may be many.
4.11: For I teach thee the ways of wisdom; and I cause thee to go in right paths.
4.12: For when thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not be distressed.
4.13: Take hold of my instruction; let it not go,—but keep it for thyself for thy life.
4.14: Go not in the ways of the ungodly, neither covet the ways of transgressors.
4.15: In whatever place they shall pitch their camp, go not thither; but turn from them, and pass away.
4.16: For they cannot sleep, unless they have done evil: their sleep is taken away, and they rest not.
4.17: For these live upon the bread of ungodliness, and are drunken with wine of transgression.
4.18: But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go on and shine, until the day be fully come.
4.19: But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they know not how they stumble.
4.20: My son, attend to my speech; and apply thine ear to my words:
4.21: that thy fountains may not fail thee; keep them in thine heart.
4.22: For they are life to those that find them, and health to all their flesh.
4.23: Keep thine heart with the utmost care; for out of these are the issues of life.
4.24: Remove from thee a froward mouth, and put far away from thee unjust lips.
4.25: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids assent to just things .
4.26: Make straight paths for thy feet, and order thy ways aright.
4.27: and he will make thy ways straight, and will guide thy steps in peace.

5.1: My son, attend to my wisdom, and apply thine ear to my words;
5.2: that thou mayest keep good understanding, and the discretion of my lips gives thee a charge. Give no heed to a worthless woman;
5.3: for honey drops from the lips of a harlot, who for a season pleases thy palate:
5.4: but afterwards thou wilt find her more bitter than gall, and sharper than a two-edged sword.
5.5: For the feet of folly lead those who deal with her down to the grave with death; and her steps are not established.
5.6: For she goes not upon the paths of life; but her ways are slippery, and not easily known.
5.7: Now then, my son, hear me, and make not my words of none effect.
5.8: Remove thy way far from her; draw not near to the doors of her house:
5.9: lest thou give away thy life to others, and thy substance to the merciless:
5.10: lest strangers be filled with thy strength, and thy labours come into the houses of strangers;
5.11: and thou repent at last, when the flesh of thy body is consumed,
5.12: and thou shalt say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart avoided reproofs!
5.13: I heard not the voice of him that instructed me, and taught me, neither did I apply mine ear.
5.14: I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.
5.15: Drink waters out of thine own vessels, and out of thine own springing wells.
5.16: Let not waters out of thy fountain be spilt by thee, but let thy waters go into thy streets.
5.17: Let them be only thine own, and let no stranger partake with thee.
5.18: Let thy fountain of water be truly thine own; and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
5.19: Let thy loving hart and thy graceful colt company with thee, and let her be considered thine own, and be with thee at all times; for ravished with her love thou shalt be greatly increased.
5.20: Be not intimate with a strange woman, neither fold thyself in the arms of a woman not thine own.
5.21: For the ways of a man are before the eyes of God, and he looks on all his paths.
5.22: Iniquities ensnare a man, and every one is bound in the chains of his own sins.
5.23: Such a man dies with the uninstructed; and he is cast forth from the abundance of his own substance, and has perished through folly.

6.1: My son, if thou become surety for thy friend, thou shalt deliver thine hand to an enemy.
6.2: For a man's own lips become a strong snare to him, and he is caught with the lips of his own mouth.
6.3: My son, do what I command thee, and deliver thyself; for on thy friend's account thou art come into the power of evil men : faint not, but stir up even thy friend for whom thou art become surety.
6.4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber with thine eyelids;
6.5: that thou mayest deliver thyself as a doe out of the toils, and as a bird out of a snare.
6.6: Go to the ant, O sluggard; and see, and emulate his ways, and become wiser than he.
6.7: For whereas he has no husbandry, nor any one to compel him, and is under no master,
6.8: whose labours kings and private men use for health, and she is desired and respected by all:
6.9: How long wilt thou lie, O sluggard? and when wilt thou awake out of sleep?
6.10: Thou sleepest a little, and thou restest a little, and thou slumberest a short time , and thou foldest thine arms over thy breast a little.
6.11: but if thou be diligent, thine harvest shall arrive as a fountain, and poverty shall flee away as a bad courier.
6.12: A foolish man and a transgressor goes in ways that are not good.
6.13: And the same winks with the eye, and makes a sign with his foot, and teaches with the beckonings of his fingers.
6.14: His perverse heart devises evils: at all times such a one causes troubles to a city.
6.15: Therefore his destruction shall come suddenly; overthrow and irretrievable ruin.
6.16: For he rejoices in all things which God hates, and he is ruined by reason of impurity of soul.
6.17: The eye of the haughty, a tongue unjust, hands shedding the blood of the just;
6.18: and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do evil,— are hateful to God .
6.19: An unjust witness kindles falsehoods, and brings on quarrels between brethren.
6.20: My son, keep the laws of thy father, and reject not the ordinances of thy mother:
6.21: but bind them upon thy soul continually, and hang them as a chain about thy neck.
6.22: Whensoever thou walkest, lead this along and let it be with thee; and when thou sleepest let it keep thee; that it may talk with thee when thou wakest.
6.23: For the commandment of the law is a lamp and a light; a way of life; reproof also and correction:
6.24: to keep thee continually from a married woman, and from the calumny of a strange tongue.
6.25: Let not the desire of beauty overcome thee, neither be thou caught by thine eyes, neither be captivated with her eyelids.
6.26: For the value of a harlot is as much as of one loaf; and a woman hunts for the precious souls of men.
6.27: Shall any one bind fire in his bosom, and not burn his garments?
6.28: or will any one walk on coals of fire, and not burn his feet?
6.29: So is he that goes in to a married woman; he shall not be held guiltless, neither any one that touches her.
6.30: It is not to be wondered at if one should be taken stealing, for he steals that when hungry he may satisfy his soul:
6.31: but if he should be taken, he shall repay sevenfold, and shall deliver himself by giving all his goods.
6.32: But the adulterer through want of sense procures destruction to his soul.
6.33: He endures both pain and disgrace, and his reproach shall never be wiped off.
6.34: For the soul of her husband is full of jealousy: he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
6.35: He will not forego his enmity for any ransom: neither will he be reconciled for many gifts.

7.1: My son, honour the Lord, and thou shalt be strong; and fear none but him:
7.2: keep my commandments, and thou shalt live; and keep my words as the pupils of thine eyes.
7.3: And bind them on thy fingers, and write them on the table of thine heart.
7.4: Say that wisdom is thy sister, and gain prudence as an acquaintance for thyself;
7.5: that she may keep thee from the strange and wicked woman, if she should assail thee with flattering words.
7.6: For she looks from a window out of her house into the streets, at one whom she may see of the senseless ones, a young man void of understanding,
7.7: passing by the corner in the passages near her house,
7.8: and speaking, in the dark of the evening,
7.9: when there happens to be the stillness of night and of darkness:
7.10: and the woman meets him having the appearance of a harlot, that causes the hearts of young men to flutter.
7.11: And she is fickle, and debauched, and her feet abide not at home.
7.12: For at one time she wanders without, and at another time she lies in wait in the streets, at every corner.
7.13: Then she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said to him,
7.14: I have a peace-offering; to-day I pay my vows:
7.15: therefore I came forth to meet thee, desiring thy face; and I have found thee.
7.16: I have spread my bed with sheets, and I have covered it with double tapestry from Egypt.
7.17: I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon.
7.18: Come, and let us enjoy love until the morning; come, and let us embrace in love.
7.19: For my husband is not at home, but is gone on a long journey,
7.20: having taken in his hand a bundle of money: after many days he will return to his house.
7.21: So with much converse she prevailed on him to go astray, and with the snares of her lips she forced him from the right path .
7.22: And he followed her, being gently led on, and that as an ox is led to the slaughter, and as a dog to bonds, or as a hart shot in the liver with an arrow:
7.23: and he hastens as a bird into a snare, not knowing that he is running for his life.
7.24: Now then, my son, hearken to me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
7.25: Let not thine heart turn aside to her ways:
7.26: for she has wounded and cast down many, and those whom she has slain are innumerable.
7.27: Her house is the way of hell, leading down to the chambers of death.

8.1: Thou shalt proclaim wisdom, that understanding may be obedient to thee.
8.2: For she is on lofty eminences, and stands in the midst of the ways.
8.3: For she sits by the gates of princes, and sings in the entrances, saying ,
8.4: You, O men, I exhort; and utter my voice to the sons of men.
8.5: O ye simple, understand subtlety, and ye that are untaught, imbibe knowledge.
8.6: Hearken to me; for I will speak solemn truths ; and will produce right sayings from my lips.
8.7: For my throat shall meditate truth; and false lips are an abomination before me.
8.8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing in them wrong or perverse.
8.9: They are all evident to those that understand, and right to those that find knowledge.
8.10: Receive instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than tried gold.
8.11: For wisdom is better than precious stones; and no valuable substance is of equal worth with it.
8.12: I wisdom have dwelt with counsel and knowledge, and I have called upon understanding.
8.13: The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, and insolence, and pride, and the ways of wicked men; and I hate the perverse ways of bad men.
8.14: Counsel and safety are mine: prudence is mine, and strength is mine.
8.15: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
8.16: By me nobles become great, and monarchs by me rule over the earth.
8.17: I love those that love me; and they that seek me shall find me .
8.18: Wealth and glory belong to me; yea, abundant possessions and righteousness.
8.19: It is better to have my fruit than to have gold and precious stones; and my produce is better than choice silver.
8.20: I walk in ways of righteousness, and am conversant with the paths of judgment;
8.21: If I declare to you the things that daily happen, I will remember also to recount the things of old.
8.22: The Lord made me the beginning of his ways for his works.
8.23: He established me before time was in the beginning, before he made the earth:
8.24: even before he made the depths; before the fountains of water came forth:
8.25: before the mountains were settled, and before all hills, he begets me.
8.26: The Lord made countries and uninhabited tracts , and the highest inhabited parts of the world.
8.27: When he prepared the heaven, I was present with him; and when he prepared his throne upon the winds:
8.28: and when he strengthened the clouds above; and when he secured the fountains of the earth:
8.29: and when he strengthened the foundations of the earth:
8.30: I was by him, suiting myself to him , I was that wherein he took delight; and daily I rejoiced in his presence continually.
8.31: For he rejoiced when he had completed the world, and rejoiced among the children of men.
8.32: Now then, my son, hear me: blessed is the man who shall hearken to me, and the mortal who shall keep my ways;
8.34: watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my entrances.
8.35: For my outgoings are the outgoings of life, and in them is prepared favour from the Lord.
8.36: But they that sin against me act wickedly against their own souls: and they that hate me love death.

9.1: Wisdom has built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars.
9.2: She has killed her beasts; she has mingled her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table.
9.3: She has sent forth her servants, calling with a loud proclamation to the feast, saying,
9.4: Whoso is foolish, let him turn aside to me: and to them that want understanding she says,
9.5: Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I have mingled for you.
9.6: Leave folly, that ye may reign for ever; and seek wisdom, and improve understanding by knowledge.
9.7: He that reproves evil men shall get dishonour to himself; and he that rebukes an ungodly man shall disgrace himself.
9.8: Rebuke not evil men , lest they should hate thee: rebuke a wise man , and he will love thee.
9.9: Give an opportunity to a wise man , and he will be wiser: instruct a just man, and he will receive more instruction .
9.10: for to know the law is the character of a sound mind.
9.11: For in this way thou shalt live long, and years of thy life shall be added to thee.
9.12: for he has forsaken the ways of his own vineyard, and he has caused the axles of his own husbandry to go astray;
9.13: A foolish and bold woman, who knows not modesty, comes to want a morsel.
9.14: She sits at the doors of her house, on a seat openly in the streets,
9.15: calling to passers by, and to those that are going right on their ways;
9.16: saying , Whoso is most senseless of you, let him turn aside to me; and I exhort those that want prudence, saying,
9.17: Take and enjoy secret bread, and the sweet water of theft.
9.18: for thus shalt thou go through strange water;

10.1: A wise son makes his father glad: but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
10.2: Treasures shall not profit the lawless: but righteousness shall deliver from death.
10.3: The Lord will not famish a righteous soul: but he will overthrow the life of the ungodly.
10.4: A son who is instructed shall be wise, and shall use the fool for a servant.
10.5: A wise son is saved from heat: but a lawless son is blighted of the winds in harvest.
10.6: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but untimely grief shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.
10.7: The memory of the just is praised; but the name of the ungodly man is extinguished.
10.8: A wise man in heart will receive commandments; but he that is unguarded in his lips shall be overthrown in his perverseness.
10.9: He that walks simply, walks confidently; but he that perverts his ways shall be known.
10.10: He that winks with his eyes deceitfully, procures griefs for men; but he that reproves boldly is a peacemaker.
10.11: There is a fountain of life in the hand of a righteous man; but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.
10.12: Hatred stirs up strife; but affection covers all that do not love strife.
10.13: He that brings forth wisdom from his lips smites the fool with a rod.
10.14: The wise will hide discretion; but the mouth of the hasty draws near to ruin.
10.15: The wealth of rich men is a strong city; but poverty is the ruin of the ungodly.
10.16: The works of the righteous produce life; but the fruits of the ungodly produce sins.
10.17: Instruction keeps the right ways of life; but instruction unchastened goes astray.
10.18: Righteous lips cover enmity; but they that utter railings are most foolish.
10.19: By a multitude of words thou shalt not escape sin; but if thou refrain thy lips thou wilt be prudent.
10.20: The tongue of the just is tried silver; but the heart of the ungodly shall fail.
10.21: The lips of the righteous know sublime truths : but the foolish die in want.
10.22: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; it enriches him , and grief of heart shall not be added to it .
10.23: A fool does mischief in sport; but wisdom brings forth prudence for a man.
10.24: The ungodly is engulphed in destruction; but the desire of the righteous is acceptable.
10.25: When the storm passes by, the ungodly vanishes away; but the righteous turns aside and escapes for ever.
10.26: As a sour grape is hurtful to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so iniquity hurts those that practise it.
10.27: The fear of the Lord adds length of days: but the years of the ungodly shall be shortened.
10.28: Joy rests long with the righteous: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
10.29: The fear of the Lord is a strong hold of the saints: but ruin comes to them that work wickedness.
10.30: The righteous shall never fail: but the ungodly shall not dwell in the earth.
10.31: The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom: but the tongue of the unjust shall perish.
10.32: The lips of just men drop grace: but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse.

11.1: False balances are an abomination before the Lord: but a just weight is acceptable unto him.
11.2: Wherever pride enters, there will be also disgrace: but the mouth of the lowly meditates wisdom.
11.3: When a just man dies he leaves regret: but the destruction of the ungodly is speedy, and causes joy.
11.5: Righteousness traces out blameless paths: but ungodliness encounters unjust dealing.
11.6: The righteousness of upright men delivers them: but transgressors are caught in their own destruction.
11.7: At the death of a just man his hope does not perish: but the boast of the ungodly perishes.
11.8: A righteous man escapes from a snare, and the ungodly man is delivered up in his place.
11.9: In the mouth of ungodly men is a snare to citizens: but the understanding of righteous men is prosperous.
11.10: In the prosperity of righteous men a city prospers:
11.11: but by the mouths of ungodly men it is overthrown.
11.12: A man void of understanding sneers at his fellow citizens: but a sensible man is quiet.
11.13: A double-tongued man discloses the secret counsels of an assembly: but he that is faithful in spirit conceals matters.
11.14: They that have no guidance fall like leaves: but in much counsel there is safety.
11.15: A bad man does harm wherever he meets a just man: and he hates the sound of safety.
11.16: A gracious wife brings glory to her husband: but a woman hating righteousness is a theme of dishonour. The slothful come to want: but the diligent support themselves with wealth.
11.17: A merciful man does good to his own soul: but the merciless destroys his own body.
11.18: An ungodly man performs unrighteous works: but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
11.19: A righteous son is born for life: but the persecution of the ungodly ends in death.
11.20: Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord: but all they that are blameless in their ways are acceptable to him.
11.21: He that unjustly strikes hands shall not be unpunished: but he that sows righteousness shall receive a faithful reward.
11.22: As an ornament in a swine's snout, so is beauty to an ill-minded woman.
11.23: All the desire of the righteous is good: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
11.24: There are some who scatter their own, and make it more: and there are some also who gather, yet have less.
11.25: Every sincere soul is blessed: but a passionate man is not graceful.
11.26: May he that hoards corn leave it to the nation: but blessing be on the head of him that gives it .
11.27: He that devises good counsels seeks good favour: but as for him that seeks after evil, evil shall overtake him.
11.28: He that trusts in wealth shall fall; but he that helps righteous men shall rise.
11.29: He that deals not graciously with his own house shall inherit the wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise man.
11.30: Out of the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life; but the souls of transgressors are cut off before their time.
11.31: If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?

12.1: He that loves instruction loves sense, but he that hates reproofs is a fool.
12.2: He that has found favour with the Lord is made better; but a transgressor shall be passed over in silence.
12.3: A man shall not prosper by wickedness; but the roots of the righteous shall not be taken up.
12.4: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a bad woman destroys her husband.
12.5: The thoughts of the righteous are true judgments; but ungodly men devise deceits.
12.6: The words of ungodly men are crafty; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
12.7: When the ungodly is overthrown, he vanishes away; but the houses of the just remain.
12.8: The mouth of an understanding man is praised by a man; but he that is dull of heart is had in derision.
12.9: Better is a man in dishonour serving himself, than one honouring himself and wanting bread.
12.10: A righteous man has pity for the lives of his cattle; but the bowels of the ungodly are unmerciful.
12.11: He that enjoys himself in banquets of wine, shall leave dishonour in his own strong holds.
12.12: The desires of the ungodly are evil; but the roots of the godly are firmly set.
12.13: He whose looks are gentle shall be pitied, but he that contends in the gates will afflict souls.
12.14: The soul of a man shall be filled with good from the fruits of his mouth; and the recompence of his lips shall be given to him.
12.15: The ways of fools are right in their own eyes; but a wise man hearkens to counsels.
12.16: A fool declares his wrath the same day; but a prudent man hides his own disgrace.
12.17: A righteous man declares the open truth; but an unjust witness is deceitful.
12.18: Some wound as they speak, like swords; but the tongues of the wise heal.
12.19: True lips establish testimony; but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue.
12.20: There is deceit in the heart of him that imagines evil; but they that love peace shall rejoice.
12.21: No injustice will please a just man; but the ungodly will be filled with mischief.
12.22: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord; but he that deals faithfully is accepted with him.
12.23: An understanding man is a throne of wisdom; but the heart of fools shall meet with curses.
12.24: The hand of chosen men shall easily obtain rule; but the deceitful shall be for a prey.
12.25: A terrible word troubles the heart of a righteous man; but a good message rejoices him.
12.26: A just arbitrator shall be his own friend; but mischief shall pursue sinners; and the way of ungodly men shall lead them astray.
12.27: A deceitful man shall catch no game; but a blameless man is a precious possession.
12.28: In the ways of righteousness is life; but the ways of those that remember injuries lead to death.

13.1: A wise son is obedient to his father: but a disobedient son will be destroyed.
13.2: A good man shall eat of the fruits of righteousness: but the lives of transgressors shall perish before their time.
13.3: He that keeps his own mouth keeps his own life: but he that is hasty with his lips shall bring terror upon himself.
13.4: Every slothful man desires, but the hands of the active are diligent.
13.5: A righteous man hates an unjust word: but an ungodly man is ashamed, and will have no confidence.
13.7: There are some who, having nothing, enrich themselves: and there are some who bring themselves down in the midst of much wealth.
13.8: A man's own wealth is the ransom of his life: but the poor endures not threatening.
13.9: Crafty souls go astray in sins: but just men pity, and are merciful.
13.10: A bad man does evil with insolence: but they that are judges of themselves are wise.
13.11: Wealth gotten hastily with iniquity is diminished: but he that gathers for himself with godliness shall be increased. The righteous is merciful, and lends.
13.12: Better is he that begins to help heartily, than he that promises and leads another to hope: for a good desire is a tree of life.
13.13: To a crafty son there shall be nothing good: but a wise servant shall have prosperous doings, and his way shall be directed aright.
13.14: The law of the wise is a fountain of life: but the man void of understanding shall die by a snare.
13.15: Sound discretion gives favour, and to know the law is the part of a sound understanding: but the ways of scorners tend to destruction.
13.16: Every prudent man acts with knowledge: but the fool displays his own mischief.
13.17: A rash king shall fall into mischief: but a wise messenger shall deliver him.
13.18: Instruction removes poverty and disgrace: but he that attends to reproofs shall be honoured.
13.19: The desires of the godly gladden the soul, but the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
13.20: If thou walkest with wise men thou shalt be wise: but he that walks with fools shall be known.
13.21: Evil shall pursue sinners; but good shall overtake the righteous.
13.22: A good man shall inherit children's children; and the wealth of ungodly men is laid up for the just.
13.23: The righteous shall spend many years in wealth: but the unrighteous shall perish suddenly.
13.24: He that spares the rod hates his son: but he that loves, carefully chastens him .
13.25: A just man eats and satisfies his soul: but the souls of the ungodly are in want.

14.1: Wise women build houses: but a foolish one digs hers down with her hands.
14.2: He that walks uprightly fears the Lord; but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonoured.
14.3: Out of the mouth of fools comes a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them.
14.4: Where no oxen are, the cribs are clean; but where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is apparent.
14.5: A faithful witness does not lie; but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods.
14.6: Thou shalt seek wisdom with bad men, and shalt not find it; but discretion is easily available with the prudent.
14.7: All things are adverse to a foolish man; but wise lips are the weapons of discretion.
14.8: The wisdom of the prudent will understand their ways; but the folly of fools leads astray.
14.9: The houses of transgressors will need purification; but the houses of the just are acceptable.
14.10: If a man's mind is intelligent, his soul is sorrowful; and when he rejoices, he has no fellowship with pride.
14.11: The houses of ungodly men shall be utterly destroyed; but the tabernacles of them that walk uprightly shall stand.
14.12: There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depth of hell.
14.13: Grief mingles not with mirth; and joy in the end comes to grief.
14.14: A stout-hearted man shall be filled with his own ways; and a good man with his own thoughts.
14.15: The simple believes every word: but the prudent man betakes himself to after-thought.
14.16: A wise man fears, and departs from evil; but the fool trusts in himself, and joins himself with the transgressor.
14.17: A passionate man acts inconsiderately; but a sensible man bears up under many things.
14.18: Fools shall have mischief for their portion; but the prudent shall take fast hold of understanding.
14.19: Evil men shall fall before the good; and the ungodly shall attend at the gates of the righteous.
14.20: Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many.
14.21: He that dishonours the needy sins: but he that has pity on the poor is most blessed.
14.22: They that go astray devise evils: but the good devise mercy and truth. The framers of evil do not understand mercy and truth: but compassion and faithfulness are with the framers of good.
14.23: With every one who is careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in want.
14.24: A prudent man is the crown of the wise: but the occupation of fools is evil.
14.25: A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evil: but a deceitful man kindles falsehoods.
14.26: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and he leaves his children a support.
14.27: The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causes men to turn aside from the snare of death.
14.28: In a populous nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of people is the ruin of a prince.
14.29: A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish.
14.30: A meek-spirited man is a healer of the heart: but a sensitive heart is a corruption of the bones.
14.31: He that oppresses the needy provokes his Maker: but he that honours him has pity upon the poor.
14.32: The ungodly shall be driven away in his wickedness: but he who is secure in his own holiness is just.
14.33: There is wisdom in the good heart of a man: but in the heart of fools it is not discerned.
14.34: Righteousness exalts a nation: but sins diminish tribes.
14.35: An understanding servant is acceptable to a king; and by his good behaviour he removes disgrace.

15.1: Anger slays even wise men; yet a submissive answer turns away wrath: but a grievous word stirs up anger.
15.2: The tongue of the wise knows what is good: but the mouth of the foolish tells out evil things.
15.3: The eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good in every place.
15.4: The wholesome tongue is a tree of life, and he that keeps it shall be filled with understanding.
15.5: A fool scorns his father's instruction: but he that keeps his commandments is more prudent. In abounding righteousness is great strength: but the ungodly shall utterly perish from the earth.
15.6: In the houses of the righteous is much strength: but the fruits of the ungodly shall perish.
15.7: The lips of the wise are bound by discretion: but the hearts of the foolish are not safe.
15.8: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord; but the prayers of them that walk honestly are acceptable with him.
15.9: The ways of an ungodly man are an abomination to the Lord; but he loves those that follow after righteousness.
15.10: The instruction of the simple is known by them that pass by; but they that hate reproofs die disgracefully.
15.11: Hell and destruction are manifest to the Lord; how shall not also be the hearts of men?
15.12: An uninstructed person will not love those that reprove him; neither will he associate with the wise.
15.13: When the heart rejoices the countenance is cheerful; but when it is in sorrow, the countenance is sad.
15.14: An upright heart seeks discretion; but the mouth of the uninstructed will experience evils.
15.15: The eyes of the wicked are always looking for evil things; but the good are always quiet.
15.16: Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without the fear of the Lord .
15.17: Better is an entertainment of herbs with friendliness and kindness, than a feast of calves, with enmity.
15.18: A man slow to anger will extinguish quarrels; but an ungodly man rather stirs them up.
15.19: The ways of sluggards are strewn with thorns; but those of the diligent are made smooth.
15.20: A wise son gladdens his father; but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
15.21: The ways of a foolish man are void of sense; but a wise man proceeds on his way aright.
15.22: They that honour not councils put off deliberation; but counsel abides in the hearts of counsellors.
15.23: A bad man will by no means attend to counsel; neither will he say anything seasonable, or good for the common weal .
15.24: The thoughts of the wise are ways of life, that he may turn aside and escape from hell.
15.25: The Lord pulls down the houses of scorners; but he establishes the border of the widow.
15.26: An unrighteous thought is abomination to the Lord; but the sayings of the pure are held in honour.
15.27: [By alms and by faithful dealings sins are purged away;] but by the fear of the Lord every one departs from evil.
15.28: The ways of righteous men are acceptable with the Lord; and through them even enemies become friends.
15.29: Let the heart of a man think justly, that his steps may be rightly ordered of God.
15.30: The eye that sees rightly rejoices the heart; and a good report fattens the bones.
15.32: He that rejects instruction hates himself; but he that minds reproofs loves his soul.
15.33: The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom; and the highest honour will correspond therewith.

16.2: All the works of the humble man are manifest with God; but the ungodly shall perish in an evil day.
